chapters.title: Chapter 401: The Silent Battle
paragraphs: And just like that a few turns passed. Camilla placed another card down and Sacha stared at it. Then she looked at Camilla with a bit of surprise on her face, "Wait."
Camilla looked up. "Yes?"
"You deliberately kept that card?"
"Yes."
"Why?"
"It was more useful than the others."
Sacha frowned. That was the obvious answer. Yet somehow, hearing Camilla say it with such complete certainty made it more irritating.
The game continued.
Because Stan and Sacha had grown up with the game, small tells still passed between them. Brief glances, tiny shifts in posture, the half-second pause before a strong play.
They had been playing together for years. Sometimes they barely needed words. Camilla noticed every one of them.
At one point Sacha saw Stan prepare a disruptive move and assumed Camilla would miss the significance.
Stan placed his card down. "Draw Two."
Camilla calmly answered with her own. "Draw Two."
Stan’s eyebrows rose.
Sacha stared at the table. "What?"
Camilla calmly continued. Stan drew the required cards.
Sacha immediately looked toward Camilla.
"That was an interesting move"
Camilla’s gaze shifted briefly toward Stan. "He looked pleased before he played the card."
Stan blinked. Sacha slowly turned toward him.
"You did look pleased."
"I wasn’t aware I had a particular expression for that."
"You absolutely do."
Camilla nodded, supporting with an expressionless face, "You do."
Stan looked at her. "You’re already analyzing my expressions?"
"Yes."
Sacha groaned.
Camilla smiled a bit at their reaction and said without the slightest hint of embarrassment. "You two told me game was competitive."
"That doesn’t mean you have to dissect us."
"I am simply observing."
Stan couldn’t help smiling. "She has a point."
Sacha glared at him. "Don’t encourage her."
"You have to admit her style is completely different from that of a newbie..."
The game continued. As the rounds progressed, Camilla’s rapid learning became impossible to ignore.
She tracked which cards had appeared, which colors had been forced, and which action cards remained unaccounted for. Predictions formed and adjusted with each new play.
Stan watched with quiet interest rather than frustration.
’She’s actually memorizing the game state.’
The sharp memory and analytical clarity impressed him. She wasn’t simply remembering cards. She was remembering sequences. She was connecting those sequences to the behavior of the players.
And whenever a prediction proved wrong, she adjusted.
She didn’t stubbornly cling to her previous assumption.
Sacha, however, looked increasingly strained. This woman learned Uno today. Why is she playing like she’s been doing this for years?
Sacha tried intimidation. "You know, being good at remembering things doesn’t mean you’re going to win."
"I am aware," Camilla answered calmly.
Sacha waited. A few turns later, Camilla executed another precise sequence.
Sacha scowled. "You’re really annoying."
"You said that about Stan earlier."
"And now I’m saying it about you."
Stan laughed under his breath.
Camilla’s mouth curved in the faintest suggestion of a smile.
Sacha pointed at both of them. "Stop enjoying this."
"I am enjoying it," Stan admitted.
"I noticed." Sacha retorted...
Camilla calmly placed another card. "That is understandable."
Sacha stared at her. "Was that supposed to be a joke?"
"No."
Stan burst out laughing. Sacha covered her face for a moment. "Why did I invite her into this game?"
"Because you thought you’d destroy her," Stan replied.
"I was confident."
"You still are."
"I’m reconsidering, that was a mistake..."
Sacha was simply unlucky, not only was her set of card this time not giving her a chance, her opponents were also merciless as well..
Camilla placed another card. "That may be wise."
Sacha slowly looked at her. "You really are enjoying this."
Camilla’s faint smile remained. "Perhaps."
The game continued. Eventually, Stan began to believe he had mapped Camilla’s patterns.
She tended to preserve certain cards. She favored particular color transitions.
She seemed reluctant to use certain action cards unless she could gain something significant from them.
Stan began constructing his plays around those observations.
He noticed that she appeared to be setting up a particular sequence.
So he made a move specifically designed to disrupt it. It worked.
Camilla was forced into the response he expected.
Stan smiled internally. ’I’ve got her.’
For several turns, his prediction remained correct. He began controlling the flow of the game again.
Sacha noticed. "Ah. There he is."
Stan looked at her. "Who?"
"My annoying little brother."
"You say that like you’re proud."
"I am."
Camilla remained silent. Her crimson eyes rested on Stan. She had noticed the change. He was becoming more confident. Not careless or reckless. Just slightly too certain that he had figured her out.
So she changed her pattern. Not dramatically, but just enough.
Instead of playing according to the behavior Stan had identified, she deliberately broke it.
Stan noticed the change. She changed her strategy.
’New age humans games are really interesting, it makes me more curious about what more they have.’ She smiled as she studied Stan, smiling when she noticed him adjusting to her change..

With that small smile, Camilla adjusted again, she can easily observe their cards with her spiritual sense, but she didn’t do it, after all, cheating in a minor game she can easily win by knowing the rules was an insult to her bloodline...
Stan himself, knew that Camilla can easily know their cards with her senses, but he knew how prideful she was, that she won’t try it...
The two of them locked eyes for about three seconds at that moment and began playing almost like a silent battle of prediction.
Sacha sat between them, increasingly confused. ’What am I even watching anymore?’
Then Camilla made a mistake. She chose the wrong color and was forced to draw on the following turn.
Sacha’s eyes immediately brightened.
"Aha!"
Camilla looked at her. "Aha?"
"You made a mistake."
"Yes."
Sacha grinned triumphantly. "So you’re not invincible after all."
"I never claimed to be."
"Good."
Sacha leaned back. "Because being good at remembering things doesn’t mean you’re going to win."
"I am aware." A few turns later, Camilla made another excellent move.
Sacha’s smile disappeared. "You’re really annoying."
Camilla looked at her. "You said that already."
Stan laughed. Sacha groaned.
"Fine. I hate playing against you two."
"You played against Stan for years," Camilla pointed out.
"Exactly, which makes his current style even more surprising since it’s completely different from his usual style..."
Stan raised an eyebrow.. Eventually, the three hands began shrinking. Sacha had three cards remaining. Stan had two and Camilla had two.

chapters.title: Chapter 402: An Unexpected Victor
paragraphs: Eventually, the three hands began shrinking. Sacha had three cards remaining. Stan had two and Camilla had two.
Sacha looked between them and realised she was about to get absolutely demolished by one of these two again...
"Wait." she said softly but neither responded.
"You two are actually taking this seriously."
Stan glanced at her. "You’re just noticing?"
Sacha shook her head. "This isn’t playing anymore. This is warfare."
Stan smiled. "You said it yourself earlier."
Sacha sighed. "Fine. Let’s see who survives."
She knew even though they were both 1 card less than hers, she still has a chance to clutch this, she wasn’t about to let it go to waste...
The next turn began and Camilla played a card. Stan studied it and immediately recognized what she was doing.
’She’s setting up the color... Huh...’
He knew what she was trying to accomplish. He had seen her preserve a particular card earlier. So he made his move. He changed the color.
Camilla paused. Then calmly drew a card. Stan smiled. ’Got her.’
But Camilla didn’t look frustrated. She simply picked up the card and added it to her hand.
The game continued. A few turns later, Stan after some up and downs was down to two cards. Camilla was also back to two.
Sacha still had three. Her heart began beating faster. ’Do I really have a chance at winning this?’
Stan glanced at Camilla’s cards. He had a fairly clear idea of what she was holding. At least, he thought he did.
He had correctly identified most of the cards in her hand throughout the game.
There was only one particular action card he believed she still possessed. He had seen the way she had played earlier. He had accounted for the cards that had appeared, so he was certain.
So when the opportunity came, he built his next move around that assumption. He changed the color.
Camilla looked at the card. Then at him. Her expression remained calm. She placed another card down.
Stan’s eyes narrowed. That wasn’t what he expected. He quickly recalculated. Then his eyes widened slightly.
’Wait. That card isn’t in her hand.’
The realization came too late. The card he had assumed Camilla was holding had already been discarded two turns earlier.
He had simply failed to account for it. Worse, Camilla had noticed that he had begun predicting her based on her previous behavior.
She had deliberately altered her pattern and allowed him to build the wrong conclusion.
Stan stared at the cards. ’She baited me.’
He thought he can easily control and outsmart Camilla the way he handled his sis... But he was given a hard slap of reality... Camilla’s intelligence and IQ wasn’t to be underestimated.
Not that he was underestimating her when this round, but he should never had allowed for that mistake.
Meanwhile, Camilla immediately exploited the opening. She placed an action card at exactly the right moment.
"Reverse."
With that, the direction changed.
Sacha blinked in complete surprise; "Wait, what?
Camilla calmly continued. She changed the color. Stan attempted to respond. He couldn’t, it was too late to do anything at this point...
Sacha was forced to draw. "What?!"
Camilla remained composed. Stan looked at the discard pile, then at Camilla’s hand.
Everything suddenly made sense. She had maneuvered both of them into positions where neither could immediately stop her.
He had been so focused on predicting her cards that he had overlooked the possibility that she had deliberately fed him false information.
Sacha looked between them; "What just happened?"
Stan smiled faintly: "I think she got us."
Camilla placed another card, "I believe that is accurate."
Sacha’s eyes widened as she gritted her teeth and said, "Don’t sound so pleased with yourself."
"I am merely stating the situation." Camilla replied calmly with an expressionless face.
Stan laughed and added, "She’s definitely pleased."
Camilla ignored him. She placed her second-to-last card down, "Uno."
Sacha’s expression changed immediately, "Wait!"
Stan looked at his own hand. Two cards. Neither could stop her.
Camilla placed her final card. It landed on the pile with a soft, decisive tap; "I believe I win."
Silence settled over the table. Sacha stared at the empty space in front of Camilla.
Then she looked at Stan, then back at Camilla, "You actually won?"
She sounded immensely disappointed in herself...
Camilla nodded once, "Yes."
"You just learned this game!"
"I did."
"And you beat both of us?"
Camilla considered the question with the same calm she had shown throughout the game, "Yes."
Sacha looked personally offended. Stan began laughing. Sacha immediately rounded on him.
"Don’t laugh! You lost too!"
He raised both hands, "I know."
"You’re laughing at your own loss?"
"I made a mistake."
Sacha blinked. "What mistake?"
Stan looked toward Camilla. "I made one wrong assumption."
Camilla met his eyes. "You underestimated me.
A small smile touched his mouth.
"Yeah. I did."
There was no embarrassment in his voice. If anything, he seemed genuinely impressed.
Camilla had proven her earlier words. She hadn’t been bluffing when she told Sacha that she believed they were underestimating her.
Sacha folded her arms, "You were both acting like geniuses five minutes ago."
Stan laughed, "And now she’s the one celebrating."
"I am not celebrating." Camilla’s expression remained perfectly composed as she said this...
Sacha pointed at her, "You’re smiling."
"Only slightly."
"That still counts."
Camilla allowed the faint smile to remain.
Then she looked at Sacha, "You said I was a newbie."
Sacha groaned, "Don’t remind me."
Camilla’s smile edged a fraction wider, "I believe I have graduated."
Stan laughed again.
Sacha pointed a finger at Camilla. "Don’t get cocky. We’re playing again."
Camilla calmly gathered the cards. "I expected that."
Recounting her immense confidence moments ago, Sacha shook her head and sighed, ’It might be newbie luck or whatever. Or maybe it’s God’s way of cutting my immense pride...’
With that, she immediately reached for the deck, "Again."
Stan nodded. "I’m in."
Camilla accepted without hesitation. "Very well."
Sacha’s hand stopped halfway to the deck.
She looked at Camilla. "No."
Stan raised an eyebrow.
"No?"
"We’re changing the system."
"What system?"
Sacha pointed directly at Camilla, "She’s not a newbie anymore."
Camilla nodded calmly. "I agree."
Sacha narrowed her eyes, "That’s exactly why I’m worried."
Stan laughed, he could tell, Sacha was trying so hard to humour the atmosphere with her jokes, considering that he and Camilla had very stiff and serious personalities...
And she was doing a really good job at that, shaking his head, he smiled and focused back at the game...

chapters.title: Chapter 403: The Battle for a Win
paragraphs: Stan laughed, he could tell, Sacha was trying so hard to humour the atmosphere with her jokes, considering that he and Camilla had very stiff and serious personalities...
And she was doing a really good job at that, shaking his head, he smiled and focused back at the game...
The three of them began preparing the next hand.
The earlier stiffness between Sacha and Camilla had almost completely dissolved, replaced by the sharp, living tension of genuine rivalry.
Somehow, a simple card game had done what hours of polite conversation could not.
Sacha no longer looked at Camilla as merely the mysterious woman who had appeared beside her brother.
Now, she looked at her as a genuine rival. And judging by the faint smile on Camilla’s face, the feeling was mutual.
Stan looked at his sister’s smile, and a warm brotherly feeling settled in his heart.

He had seen that competitive spark in her eyes before. It reminded him of the days when the two of them had little more than each other, when a simple game of Uno had been enough to make them forget, even for a little while, about everything they were going through.
He couldn’t help but smile. ’I can’t let Sis leave without winning at least one game.’
He decided then that he would help her in every way he could.
Without cheating, of course. That would defeat the entire purpose. But helping her while remaining her opponent was going to be difficult. Fortunately, he already had a plan.
Unbeknownst to Camilla, the next round had quietly become a two-versus-one battle.
Stan’s goal wasn’t to win. It was to make sure Camilla didn’t win.
He would subtly disrupt her plays whenever possible, manipulate the flow of the game to Sacha’s advantage, and create opportunities for his sister without making it obvious that he was doing so.
If Sacha happened to win in the process, perfect. If she didn’t, well... He would simply keep trying.
’Unless Sis’s luck is unbelievably terrible and I’m somehow forced into a position where my final card leaves me no choice but to win, I should be able to pull this off.’
He was confident in his ability to control the game without directly giving Sacha an obvious advantage.
Still, Stan wasn’t foolish enough to underestimate Camilla a second time. She had already proven how quickly she could adapt.
Even knowing exactly what he intended to do, winning against her would have been difficult.
And this time, she wouldn’t be playing as a newcomer. She had already experienced a full game. She understood the rules. She had studied both of them.
More importantly, she now knew what Stan was capable of.
’This won’t be easy.’
His gaze briefly shifted toward Camilla. She was calmly arranging her cards, seemingly unaware of the little scheme taking shape across the table.
’The chances of Camilla winning are still pretty high.’ Stan’s smile deepened slightly. ’That only makes things more interesting. Because this time, I’m not playing for myself.’
He glanced at Sacha. She was already preparing for the next round, that familiar competitive smile still on her face.
’Let’s see if I can get my sister a win.’
Meanwhile, Sacha gathered the cards with a satisfied little smile, clearly enjoying the fact that the previous round had ended with Camilla’s victory.
She shuffled the deck several times before looking up. "This time, I’m dealing."
Camilla nodded. "Very well."
Stan leaned back slightly as Sacha began distributing the cards.
His eyes moved between the two women. Unlike the previous round, he wasn’t thinking about how to win.
His objective was much simpler. ’Sis needs a win.’
He glanced at Sacha. She was already looking far too pleased with herself.
Then his eyes shifted toward Camilla. She sat with the same composed posture as before, her crimson eyes following every card that Sacha placed on the table.
’If I directly help Sis, Camilla will notice. If I play too badly, Sis will notice. And if I keep targeting Camilla, both of them will notice.’
Stan’s lips curled into the faintest smile. ’So I need to make every move look like something I’d naturally do while trying to win.’
That was the difficult part. He wasn’t simply playing Uno anymore. He was playing Uno while pretending he wasn’t playing a different game entirely.
Sacha finished dealing and placed the remaining deck in the middle. "Everyone ready?"
"I am," Camilla answered.
Stan nodded, "Let’s go."
The first card was turned over. The game began. At first, everything proceeded normally.
Sacha quickly established the rhythm she was comfortable with, playing aggressively whenever she saw an opportunity to reduce her hand.
Camilla was the opposite. She took her time. She studied the discard pile. She studied the cards in her hand.
And, more importantly, she watched the choices everyone else made.
Stan noticed immediately and shook his head, ’She’s already getting better.’
He wasn’t surprised after all, Camilla’s ability to absorb information was frightening.
After only one round, she had already developed an understanding of the game’s basic rhythm. Now she was beginning to understand the players.
Sacha placed another card down. "Looks like this round might actually go my way."
Stan glanced at her, "Don’t celebrate too early."
Camilla placed down her own card, "That would be premature."
Sacha stopped. Her eyes moved between them, "Why do you two suddenly sound like you’re teaming up against me?"
Stan answered immediately, "I’m not teaming up with anyone."
"Neither am I," Camilla added.
Sacha narrowed her eyes, "Then why does it feel like both of you are trying to lecture me?"
Stan shrugged, "Maybe you’re just imagining things."
"I’m not."
Camilla calmly added, "She may not be."
Stan looked at her, "Whose side are you on?"
Camilla’s face was expressionless as she replied bluntly, "My own."
Sacha immediately laughed, "Finally, someone honest."
Stan smiled faintly. ’If only you knew.’

chapters.title: Chapter 404: A Quiet Battle Of Wits
paragraphs: The game continued. A few turns later, Sacha had managed to reduce her hand considerably.
Camilla had several cards remaining, but Stan could already see the direction she was trying to take the game.
She was preserving certain cards. She was carefully maintaining multiple colors.
And judging by the way she had played the last few turns, she was preparing for a sequence that could potentially leave her with only two cards.
Stan considered his options. He could interfere directly. But that would be too obvious.
Instead, he chose a card that benefited his own hand while forcing the color into one Camilla was least likely to have.
Camilla stared at the card. Then at him and said softly, "Interesting."
Stan raised an eyebrow, "What?"
"Nothing." She replied and played her next card.
Stan’s expression remained unchanged. But internally, he was more alert.
’She noticed, or maybe she’s just getting a feeling.’ he sighed, he definitely couldn’t afford to get careless.
A few turns later, Sacha reached three cards. Camilla had four. Stan had five. Camilla’s next move made her intention clear.
She was positioning herself for a strong finish. Stan immediately recognized the danger.
He needed to interfere. But rather than targeting her directly, he played a card that looked like an attempt to improve his own position.
The result, however, forced Camilla to draw while leaving the color favorable for Sacha.
Sacha immediately seized the opportunity. Her next card hit the table and she smiled, "Nice."
Stan kept his expression neutral. ’Perfect.’
Camilla’s crimson eyes shifted toward him. They remained there for a second longer than necessary.
Stan pretended not to notice. He calmly drew his next card.
’She’s suspicious.’ He sighed, at this point it was pretty obvious that he needed to change his rhythm.
So on his next turn, he made a completely neutral play. No advantage for Sacha. No deliberate attack on Camilla. Just a reasonable move.
Camilla’s eyes narrowed slightly and the game continued. But something had changed.
Camilla was watching Stan now. Not constantly. That would have been too obvious.
Instead, she observed him between turns. His hands. His expressions.
The cards he hesitated over. The cards he played without hesitation.
She was gathering information.
Stan noticed, he was at alert he wasn’t about to miss that...
’She’s studying me... huh.’
A faint amusement appeared in his eyes. ’All right.’
Let’s see who can read whom. Camilla deliberately played a particular color. Stan recognized the choice.
It wasn’t the strongest move available to her. It was a test. She wanted to see whether he would react.
Stan understood immediately. Instead of taking the obvious opportunity, he played a different card.
Camilla’s eyes flickered. She had expected something else.
Stan leaned back. ’Nice try.’
Camilla continued playing as though nothing had happened. But internally, she had already revised her assessment.
He noticed. The next few turns became a quiet battle between them.
Neither said anything. Neither needed to. Camilla would make a move. Stan would recognize the intention behind it. He would then adjust.
She would notice the adjustment. Then she would change her approach.
Sacha, meanwhile, continued playing without realizing that the real battle was taking place between the two people sitting across from her.
Eventually, she placed another card down and glanced between them.
"Why do you two look like you’re planning a military operation?"
Stan looked at her, "It’s Uno."
"That isn’t an answer."
Camilla calmly nodded, "She is correct."
Stan turned toward Camilla, "Seriously?"
"My observation was merely factual."
Sacha laughed, "You know what? I like her."
Stan shook his head. ’This is getting dangerous.’
Sacha’s attention returned to her cards. "Anyway, I’m winning."
"You have four cards," Stan pointed out.
"And you have five."
"Exactly."
"So I’m winning."
Stan stared at her, "That isn’t how winning works."
"It is when I’m better than you." Sacha replied...
He almost laughed. She’s really getting confident. Yet beneath the teasing, Stan was pleased.
Sacha was genuinely improving. She was remembering which colors had appeared and which action cards had already been played. She had begun recognizing Camilla’s habits too.
At one point, Camilla attempted to force a particular color.
Sacha immediately countered..Camilla’s eyes flickered toward her.
Sacha grinned, "Thought you had me?"
Camilla calmly replied, "I was testing you."
Sacha’s smile froze.."...You were?"
"Yes."
Sacha’s eyes narrowed, "Don’t do that."
Camilla’s lips lifted slightly, "I’ll keep that in mind."
Stan couldn’t help smiling. ’Nice one, Sis.’
That move hadn’t been part of his plan. She had figured it out herself. The game continued.
Soon Sacha was down to three cards. Camilla had four and Stan had four.
Camilla’s position was becoming dangerous again. She had quietly accumulated the cards she needed for a strong finish.
Stan noticed. He also noticed something else. Camilla had intentionally left herself vulnerable.
It was subtle, almost too subtle. But Stan caught it. That’s a trap. If he attacked her directly, she would learn that he was paying special attention to her.
If he ignored the opening, she would learn that too. So he chose a third option. He played a card that didn’t significantly benefit either of them.
Camilla looked at him. "You didn’t take the opportunity."
Stan shrugged. "It wasn’t worth it."
She studied him. "You could have disrupted me."
"I could have."
"Yet you didn’t."
Stan calmly drew a card. "I had a better move."
Camilla said nothing. But her eyes remained on him for another moment.
’He’s hiding something.’ She didn’t know what, she couldn’t prove anything. But her instincts were telling her that Stan wasn’t playing this round the same way he had played the previous one.
Stan noticed the slight change in her expression.
’That was close.’ He sighed inwardly... He needed to be even more careful.
The game accelerated from that point, Cards moved across the table. Colors changed. Draw cards appeared and disappeared.
Sacha was now playing with far more confidence than she had at the beginning. Camilla was becoming increasingly difficult to predict.
And Stan was quietly manipulating the entire flow without ever allowing himself to make the same kind of move twice.
Eventually, Sacha reached two cards. Camilla reached two as well. Stan had three. He immediately recognized the danger.
Camilla is one good turn away. He looked at Sacha. Then at Camilla.
His mind raced through the cards that had already appeared.
He knew what Camilla was likely holding. He also knew what Sacha probably had. But he couldn’t act as though he knew.
He needed to make the correct move for the wrong-looking reason. Stan placed his card down.
Camilla’s eyes narrowed. She understood what the move accomplished. It disrupted her. But it didn’t look intentional. At least, not completely.
Sighing, she changed the color and Sacha immediately countered.
Stan watched the exchange carefully. ’Good.’
Camilla drew. Sacha’s hand dropped to one card. Her eyes widened.
She immediately straightened. "Uno!"
Stan’s heart lifted. ’Perfect.’
Camilla’s expression remained calm. She studied the table. Then her cards. She was already searching for a way to prevent Sacha from finishing.
Stan saw it too. He couldn’t let her..But if he directly stopped Camilla again, she would know.
He considered the possibilities. Then he made a move that appeared to be purely self-serving.
Camilla’s eyes shifted toward him. For half a second, she seemed to understand. Then Sacha seized the opening.
She placed her final card on the table.
Silence descended on them all...
Sacha stared at it. Then at the other two. Her eyes widened, then a grin slowly spread across her face as she said softly, "I won."

chapters.title: Chapter 405: Three Minds
paragraphs: Sacha’s eyes widened, then a grin slowly spread across her face as she said softly, "I won."
Stan leaned back and Sacha suddenly threw both hands into the air.
"Yes!"
She laughed, looking first at Camilla and then at Stan.
"You two weren’t able to beat me this round after all!"
She looked particularly pleased with herself, "Finally I’ve won!"
Stan simply smiled. He said nothing. Inside, however, he felt a quiet satisfaction.
’I did it. Sis won.’
And that was all he had wanted. He didn’t care that he had technically played a weaker game. He didn’t care that his own hand had been deliberately kept in an awkward position.
Seeing his sister’s genuine happiness was worth it. Sacha was still celebrating when Stan noticed that Camilla hadn’t moved.
Her crimson eyes were fixed directly on him. Not angry or accusing. Just intensely observant.
Stan’s smile faded slightly. He already knew what that look meant. She had felt it. She just hadn’t figured it out.
Camilla finally spoke. "You played strangely this round."
Stan raised an eyebrow. "Did I?"
"Yes you did."
Sacha looked between them. "What do you mean?"
Camilla didn’t answer immediately. Her gaze remained fixed on Stan as she said softly to him, "I haven’t determined it yet."
Stan smiled casually, "Then I guess you’ll have to keep playing."
Camilla’s eyes narrowed slightly, "Perhaps."
Sacha looked between them again, "Wait, what are you two talking about?"
"Nothing," Stan answered.
Camilla gave him a brief glance, "Nothing yet."
Stan’s expression twitched.
Sacha stared at them, "Why does that sound ominous?"
Neither answered. Sacha eventually shrugged and gathered her cards, still wearing the satisfied smile of someone who had just reclaimed her dignity.
Stan looked at her. ’One win is enough for you, Sis.’
His gaze shifted toward Camilla. She was still watching him.
’I’ll try to win next time.’
A faint smile appeared on his lips. And I definitely won’t underestimate her again. For the moment, however, he was content.
The awkwardness that had filled the apartment earlier was almost completely gone.
Sacha no longer seemed particularly concerned about Camilla being a mysterious stranger.
Camilla, meanwhile, had apparently found herself a new source of entertainment.
And Stan had a feeling that Uno was about to become far more competitive than he had ever imagined.
Sacha suddenly slapped the deck against the table. "Again."
Stan looked at her.
"Again?"
"Of course."
She pointed at Camilla. "I can’t let her have two wins."
Camilla calmly gathered her cards. "I agree.
Sacha blinked. "You agree?"
"Yes."
Camilla’s faint smile returned, "I want another game."
Stan looked at the two women. Then at the cards and then he sighed inwardly. ’This is going to get complicated.’
Sacha gathered the scattered cards and began shuffling, the satisfaction of her previous victory still lingering on her face.
She glanced at Stan with a smug little smile.
"Don’t think too much brother, it’s useless."
Stan raised an eyebrow. "But you just won the last round..."
"Exactly."
She smiled wider. "That was proof that I can still beat you."
Stan chuckled. "So that’s what you’re taking from it?"
"What else am I supposed to take from it?"
"That you got lucky?"
Sacha’s smile immediately disappeared, "Lucky?"
Stan could already see the danger in her expression.
"I’m just saying—"
"Don’t."
She pointed a card at him, "I beat you. Fair and square."
Stan laughed. "Alright, alright. I won’t take that away from you."
Sacha nodded in satisfaction and continued shuffling.
"Good. Now prepare yourself, because I’m winning again."
Her eyes was filled with determination as she added... "I’ll definitely win this round..."
Stan chuckled. "So you’re already planning your next victory?"
"Of course. Did you think that one win was going to satisfy me?"
"I suppose I should have known better."
Sacha pointed a card at him teasingly. "You’d better take me seriously this time, little brother."
Stan’s lips curled into a faint smile. "I always take you seriously."
"Liar."
"What?"
"You’re smiling."
"So?"
"You only smile like that when you think you’ve already figured something out."
Stan laughed. "You’ve known me for too long."
"Exactly."

Across from them, Camilla quietly watched the exchange, crimson eyes moving between the siblings. Their familiarity was obvious. They could read small changes in each other’s expressions and tone almost instinctively, the result of years spent together.
Unlike the previous round, however, Camilla had no intention of allowing that familiarity to become an advantage she couldn’t overcome.
Her gaze settled briefly on Stan. ’This time, I will not underestimate him either.’
Stan caught the look. For a moment, their eyes met.
Neither said anything. Sacha looked between them and sighed.
"Why do I suddenly feel like I’m about to regret starting another round?"
Stan and Camilla answered almost simultaneously.
"You probably should."
Sacha’s eyes widened. "...You two are already annoying me."

Camilla watched the exchange quietly, crimson eyes moving between the siblings. She had already noticed how naturally they understood one another. Their years of playing together had given them an advantage that simply learning the rules could not provide.
Sacha finished shuffling and dealt the cards. Stan picked up his hand and studied it.
This time, there was no hidden objective, no secret plan and no intention of helping one player over another.
’I’m winning this one.’ His gaze shifted toward Camilla. ’And I’m not making the mistake of underestimating her again.’
Then he glanced at Sacha. ’Or Sis.’

With that, the game began. Unlike the previous rounds, Stan didn’t rely solely on his enhanced perception. He combined everything at his disposal. His memory, his heightened senses, his ability to recognize patterns, and the experience he had gained from the earlier games all worked together.
He tracked every card that appeared. He remembered the colors each woman seemed to favor.
He watched their expressions. Even the slightest hesitation before a card was played was enough to provide information.
Sacha noticed almost immediately. She narrowed her eyes. "Why are you staring at my face?"
Stan didn’t look away. "I’m playing Uno."
"That doesn’t answer my question."
Camilla calmly placed a card down. "He is analyzing you."
Sacha turned toward her. "You’re helping him?"
Camilla shook her head. "No. I’m analyzing him."
Stan looked between the two women. "Wonderful. I’m surrounded."
Sacha snorted and the game continued.
Stan soon discovered that his sister had something he hadn’t fully accounted for.

She knew him, not just his playing style, but him. She knew the way he behaved when he had a strong hand. She knew the tiny changes in his expression when he was holding an action card. She even remembered certain habits from their childhood that he had long since stopped thinking about.
At one point, Stan hesitated for barely a fraction of a second before choosing a card.
Seeing the hesitation as a sign of weakness, Sacha smiled and immediately placed one down. "Got you."
Stan stared at her. "You remembered that?"
"You’ve been making that face since you were ten."
Camilla’s eyes moved between them. "You two have really known each other for a long time."
Sacha smiled. "Yes, Long enough to know when this idiot is pretending not to have a good card."
Stan sighed. "I’m beginning to regret teaching you Uno."
Camilla’s lips lifted slightly. "Your regret is understandable."
Stan glanced at her. "Whose side are you on?"
"My own."
Sacha laughed. "Finally, someone honest."

sentences.text: Sacha’s eyes widened, then a grin slowly spread across her face as she said softly, "I won."
Stan leaned back and Sacha suddenly threw both hands into the air.
"Yes!"
She laughed, looking first at Camilla and then at Stan.
"You two weren’t able to beat me this round after all!"
She looked particularly pleased with herself, "Finally I’ve won!"
Stan simply smiled.
He said nothing.
Inside, however, he felt a quiet satisfaction.
’I did it.
Sis won.’
And that was all he had wanted.
He didn’t care that he had technically played a weaker game.
He didn’t care that his own hand had been deliberately kept in an awkward position.
Seeing his sister’s genuine happiness was worth it.
Sacha was still celebrating when Stan noticed that Camilla hadn’t moved.
Her crimson eyes were fixed directly on him.
Not angry or accusing.
Just intensely observant.
Stan’s smile faded slightly.
He already knew what that look meant.
She had felt it.
She just hadn’t figured it out.
Camilla finally spoke.
"You played strangely this round."
Stan raised an eyebrow.
"Did I?"
"Yes you did."
Sacha looked between them.
"What do you mean?"
Camilla didn’t answer immediately.
Her gaze remained fixed on Stan as she said softly to him, "I haven’t determined it yet."
Stan smiled casually, "Then I guess you’ll have to keep playing."
Camilla’s eyes narrowed slightly, "Perhaps."
Sacha looked between them again, "Wait, what are you two talking about?"
"Nothing," Stan answered.
Camilla gave him a brief glance, "Nothing yet."
Stan’s expression twitched.
Sacha stared at them, "Why does that sound ominous?"
Neither answered.
Sacha eventually shrugged and gathered her cards, still wearing the satisfied smile of someone who had just reclaimed her dignity.
Stan looked at her. ’One win is enough for you, Sis.’
His gaze shifted toward Camilla.
She was still watching him.
’I’ll try to win next time.’
A faint smile appeared on his lips.
And I definitely won’t underestimate her again.
For the moment, however, he was content.
The awkwardness that had filled the apartment earlier was almost completely gone.
Sacha no longer seemed particularly concerned about Camilla being a mysterious stranger.
Camilla, meanwhile, had apparently found herself a new source of entertainment.
And Stan had a feeling that Uno was about to become far more competitive than he had ever imagined.
Sacha suddenly slapped the deck against the table.
"Again."
Stan looked at her.
"Again?"
"Of course."
She pointed at Camilla.
"I can’t let her have two wins."
Camilla calmly gathered her cards.
"I agree.
Sacha blinked.
"You agree?"
"Yes."
Camilla’s faint smile returned, "I want another game."
Stan looked at the two women.
Then at the cards and then he sighed inwardly. ’This is going to get complicated.’
Sacha gathered the scattered cards and began shuffling, the satisfaction of her previous victory still lingering on her face.
She glanced at Stan with a smug little smile.
"Don’t think too much brother, it’s useless."
Stan raised an eyebrow.
"But you just won the last round..."
"Exactly."
She smiled wider.
"That was proof that I can still beat you."
Stan chuckled.
"So that’s what you’re taking from it?"
"What else am I supposed to take from it?"
"That you got lucky?"
Sacha’s smile immediately disappeared, "Lucky?"
Stan could already see the danger in her expression.
"I’m just saying—"
"Don’t."
She pointed a card at him, "I beat you.
Fair and square."
Stan laughed.
"Alright, alright.
I won’t take that away from you."
Sacha nodded in satisfaction and continued shuffling.
"Good.
Now prepare yourself, because I’m winning again."
Her eyes was filled with determination as she added...
"I’ll definitely win this round..."
Stan chuckled.
"So you’re already planning your next victory?"
"Of course.
Did you think that one win was going to satisfy me?"
"I suppose I should have known better."
Sacha pointed a card at him teasingly.
"You’d better take me seriously this time, little brother."
Stan’s lips curled into a faint smile.
"I always take you seriously."
"Liar."
"What?"
"You’re smiling."
"So?"
"You only smile like that when you think you’ve already figured something out."
Stan laughed.
"You’ve known me for too long."
"Exactly."

Unlike the previous round, however, Camilla had no intention of allowing that familiarity to become an advantage she couldn’t overcome.
Her gaze settled briefly on Stan. ’This time, I will not underestimate him either.’
Stan caught the look.
For a moment, their eyes met.
Neither said anything.
Sacha looked between them and sighed.
"Why do I suddenly feel like I’m about to regret starting another round?"
Stan and Camilla answered almost simultaneously.
"You probably should."
Sacha’s eyes widened.
"...You two are already annoying me."

Their years of playing together had given them an advantage that simply learning the rules could not provide.

This time, there was no hidden objective, no secret plan and no intention of helping one player over another.

paragraphs: The game continued to escalate. Camilla had also changed considerably since the first round.
She no longer played like someone learning a new game. She had begun exploiting the very familiarity that existed between the siblings.
She realized that Stan and Sacha unconsciously reacted to one another.
A glance. A slight movement. A pause. A tiny shift in expression. Those things could reveal more than the cards themselves.
So she began deliberately creating situations designed to trigger those reactions.
She changed colors unexpectedly, forcing Sacha to abandon a planned move.
Later, she paused deliberately before playing an otherwise harmless card, watching Stan’s face to see whether he would react.
’He didn’t.’ Camilla’s lips curved faintly. ’He saw through it.’
Stan noticed the tiny smile.
’She’s testing me.’ The thought amused him. ’She’s getting faster.’
The three of them continued trading moves. Sacha forced Camilla to draw and Camilla immediately turned the situation around and forced Stan to draw.
Stan changed the color to one Sacha clearly didn’t want and she countered with a Wild. Camilla responded with an action card that disrupted both of their plans.
The game had stopped feeling like a casual family pastime. It had become a genuine battle of observation and prediction.
Sacha suddenly threw both hands up. "You know what? I would’ve liked it better if Camilla played like an actual newbie that’s just learning uno."
Camilla calmly placed another card down, "I admire your deep thirst for victory, but there’s no chance of you this round."
Stan smiled at the friendly rivalry, with that the game continued.

Sacha was not simply being carried by experience. She tracked which cards had already appeared, remembered the colors Camilla had been avoiding, and began recognizing some of Camilla’s tendencies from the previous round.
At one point, Sacha made a sequence that Stan hadn’t anticipated.
His eyes widened slightly. ’Nice one, Sis.’
She was genuinely improving. Any victory she achieved today would not simply be because of him.
Eventually, the game entered its final stage. Sacha had three cards. Camilla had two. Stan had two.
Stan’s eyes narrowed slightly. Camilla was dangerously close to winning again.
But still, he didn’t rush, he considered every possibility.
If he attacked Camilla directly, Sacha could potentially exploit the opening.
If he targeted Sacha, Camilla could finish. If he played defensively, both women might overtake him.
So he chose the move that gave him the greatest chance of surviving regardless of what either of them held.
The card hit the discard pile.
Camilla’s planned sequence collapsed. Her crimson eyes narrowed.
Sacha immediately tried to capitalize. Stan countered her as well.
Sacha frowned, "You’re annoying."
"You’ve said that already."
"And I’ll keep saying it."
Camilla placed another card down. "So will I."
Stan looked at both women, "You guys are ganging up on me."
Neither answered and the game continued. Eventually, all three were down to their final cards. Sacha looked between them.
"Whoever loses this one isn’t allowed to complain."
Camilla nodded. "Agreed."
Stan smiled. "Agreed."
Sacha played.
Camilla countered and Stan watched carefully.
Camilla attempted to force the color toward one she believed he couldn’t answer.
Stan calmly placed his counter..Sacha immediately tried to take advantage of the opening.
Stan countered again..Camilla’s eyes sharpened. She understood what he was doing.
She changed her approach and attempted one final reversal.
Stan had already anticipated it. His final card slid onto the pile.
Silence descended from that point...
Stan leaned back, "I win."
Both women froze. Sacha and Camilla stared at the cards..
Then, almost simultaneously, both slowly raised their heads and looked at him. They said nothing, they simply stared intently, his victory had hit them hard
Stan looked from one to the other. A second passed. Then another.
The intensity of their expressions became so ridiculous that he couldn’t hold it anymore.
He burst out laughing. "What?"
Sacha continued staring at him as though he had somehow committed an offense.
Camilla’s expression remained perfectly composed, but her crimson eyes stayed fixed on him.
Stan couldn’t help feeling a little smug. ’Finally. I have done it.’
He had refused to underestimate either of them, calculated every move carefully, and managed to take the victory.
But just as his amusement began settling, something changed.
His smile faded. His enhanced senses caught something. Stan turned toward Sacha. Then toward the air around her.
Then back to her. His eyes widened as he confirmed what he just sensed
"What... ?" Sacha sensed his intense gaze and asked...
Stan was unable to answer her after all he could sense it
The thing moving through the atmosphere, Qi. Very faint and lmost imperceptible, yet unmistakable was slowly gathering around Sacha.
More importantly, it wasn’t being rejected. It was entering her body. Her breathing remained completely normal. She didn’t appear to have noticed anything.
Her body was simply absorbing the Qi naturally.
’Impossible.’ Stan was in shock as he stared at her, or rather the QI gathering to her, "But how is she able to interact with Qi?"
His thoughts raced. ’She’s comprehended Dao.’
His system had rarely answered questions that didn’t directly concern him. Yet this time, a translucent panel suddenly appeared within his vision.
[Analysis Complete.]
[Your Sister has comprehended Dao.]
[Comprehension of Dao is the prerequisite for interacting with Qi.]
[The comprehension of Dao does not require knowledge of the word "Dao," nor does it require conscious awareness of its existence.]
[Dao is a principle of existence.]
[To comprehend Dao is to perceive, understand, and resonate with such a principle.]
[Your Sister’s understanding reached the required threshold naturally.]
[Although she does not know what Dao is, not does she know the Dao language, her soul has already recognized and comprehended one.]
[As a result, her body has gained the ability to perceive, attract, and absorb Qi.]
[She has entered the Awakening Phase.]
[The Qi she absorbs is currently tempering her body and meridians.]
[Her Dantian has yet to form.]
[Once her body has been sufficiently tempered, the accumulated Qi will naturally converge and form her Dantian.]
[In simple terms:]
[She understood Dao before she understood the concept of Dao.]
[Knowledge of the name is unnecessary but Understanding is sufficient.]
Stan remained silent. ’Damn. So this is possible?!’

chapters.title: Chapter 407: The First Resonance...
paragraphs: [Knowledge of the name is unnecessary but Understanding is sufficient.]
Stan remained silent. ’Damn. So this is possible?!’
The revelation was staggering. People didn’t necessarily need to know the word Dao or dao language to interact with Qi. They didn’t even need to understand cultivation.
If they naturally understood and resonated with a principle of existence deeply enough, their souls could comprehend Dao before their minds ever became aware of the concept.
And Sacha had apparently done exactly that.
Stan was still processing the information when he felt another gaze.
He looked up. Camilla was staring directly at him. Their eyes met.
’So she had sensed it too.’ he sighed...
Her vampire senses were far more sensitive than those of an ordinary human. She could feel the faint energy gathering around Sacha, the subtle flow of Qi entering her body.
’That energy...’ Camilla’s crimson eyes narrowed. ’It is gathering around her. She’s going through that stage, it’s been only a few hours at most
She watched Sacha carefully. She is absorbing it. There was no rejection. No discomfort..No resistance. She isn’t rejecting it.
Camilla’s gaze shifted back to Stan.
His expression had changed. She immediately understood that he hadn’t expected this.
So even he did not know this was possible. That realization was more interesting than the phenomenon itself.
Camilla remained silent, continuing to observe. Sacha eventually noticed the two of them staring at each other.
She sighed. "Why are you two locking eyes like some lovebirds?"
Stan and Camilla both stiffened.
Sacha rolled her eyes. "Seriously."
Stan cleared his throat and Camilla looked away.
Sacha shook her head before gathering her handbag. "Anyways, it was nice playing with you two. I really enjoyed the game."
She stood. "I’ll be leaving now."
Then she smiled. "It’s good that the game ended with everyone winning. No hard feelings, right?"
Stan and Camilla both gave slightly stiff nods. Neither had completely recovered from what they had just sensed.
Sacha turned toward Stan. "It’s a good thing I was able to have some quality time with you, brother. I’ll make up the time and visit you later."
"Okay, Sis." But inwardly, Stan immediately turned his attention toward the system.
’Is it okay for me to have her out of sight?’
The system responded almost immediately.
[The Supreme Rebate System knows you have no inappropriate thoughts toward your sister.]
[She will receive the same protection treatment as your harem.]
[You will be able to sense when she is frightened or in danger.]
Stan’s eyes softened. ’Really? That’s good then.’
The system continued. [This is one of the functions granted by the Harem feature during the previous upgrade.]
Stan relaxed slightly. At least if something happened to Sacha, he would know before hand since he’ll be able to tell from her emotions first...
Before leaving, Sacha casually walked over to Camilla and gave her a light pat on the shoulder.
Camilla stiffened slightly at the unexpected contact. Sacha noticed but simply smiled warmly.
Then she turned toward Stan and hugged him.
"Goodbye, Stan."
Stan hugged her back. "Goodbye, Sis."
She pulled away and looked at him with a knowing expression. "I know you’re doing well for yourself now and everything, but it’ll still be good for you to take your certificate seriously too."
Stan immediately understood why she had said certificate rather than studies.

Sacha knew him well enough to understand that, after everything he had accomplished over the past few weeks, conventional education was probably no longer at the top of his priorities, that’s why she said certificate and not education..
Stan smiled. "Don’t worry, Sis. I’ve got that covered."
Sacha shook her head with a smile. She could tell what’s going through his mind, "You cheeky boy. Knowledge is important too."
Stan laughed. "I understand, Sis."
Sacha then turned toward the door. "Come on. See me out."
Stan nodded. "Sure."
He followed her. To his mild surprise, Camilla casually followed them as well.
Stan noticed but didn’t say anything.
With that, the three of them entered the elevator.
Sacha leaned casually against the wall, glancing between her brother and Camilla. "So, Camilla."
Camilla looked toward her. "Yes?"
"You know, I think you might be the only person who can tolerate him now."
Stan’s expression changed. "Hey."
Camilla considered the statement. "I have not made that determination yet."
Sacha burst out laughing.
Stan looked at Camilla in disbelief. "You too?"
A faint smile appeared on her lips. Sacha pointed at him. "See? You’re doomed."
The elevator doors opened. They continued through the building and eventually reached the entrance.
Outside, Sacha looked around and soon spotted a taxi approaching.
She raised her hand. The taxi slowed and stopped near the gate.
Before getting inside, she turned toward Stan. "Goodbye, brother..."
She paused. Then her eyes moved toward Camilla.
A mischievous smile spread across her face. "...and my brother’s beloved."
Camilla froze and Stan noticed immediately.
Sacha’s smile widened. "I hope you two stay good together. Take good care of each other, alright?"
Camilla’s cheeks immediately flushed. She turned her face toward the side.
Sacha looked delighted. "Bye!"
She stepped into the taxi and Stan waved at her...
"Bye, Sis."
The taxi pulled away.
Stan lowered his hand and glanced toward Camilla. She was still looking to the side.
Her expression was unusually stiff, and the faint crimson coloring high on her cheeks had not disappeared.
Stan didn’t need enhanced senses to figure it out. She’s blushing.
And judging from how deliberately she refused to look at him, she was probably far more embarrassed than she wanted to admit.
Stan suppressed a laugh.
Camilla finally spoke without looking at him, "Your sister is... troublesome."
Stan laughed softly. "She likes teasing people."
Camilla remained silent for a moment. Then she muttered, "She is too bold."
Stan looked at her with amusement, "She’s my sister."
Camilla finally glanced at him, "True."
A small smile tugged at Stan’s lips as they turned back toward the building.
Yet beneath the amusement, his thoughts returned to what he had discovered.
Sacha had comprehended Dao. She had begun absorbing Qi.
Her cultivation path had already started, even though she didn’t know the first thing about cultivation.
And somehow, that realization felt like the beginning of something much bigger.
Stan looked toward the building ahead. ’Sis... what exactly did you comprehend?’

Sacha knew him well enough to understand that, after everything he had accomplished over the past few weeks, conventional education was probably no longer at the top of his priorities, that’s why she said certificate and not education..
Stan smiled.
"Don’t worry, Sis.
I’ve got that covered."
Sacha shook her head with a smile.
She could tell what’s going through his mind, "You cheeky boy.
Knowledge is important too."
Stan laughed.
"I understand, Sis."
Sacha then turned toward the door.
"Come on.
See me out."
Stan nodded.
"Sure."
He followed her.
To his mild surprise, Camilla casually followed them as well.
Stan noticed but didn’t say anything.
With that, the three of them entered the elevator.
Sacha leaned casually against the wall, glancing between her brother and Camilla.
"So, Camilla."
Camilla looked toward her.
"Yes?"
"You know, I think you might be the only person who can tolerate him now."
Stan’s expression changed.
"Hey."
Camilla considered the statement.
"I have not made that determination yet."
Sacha burst out laughing.
Stan looked at Camilla in disbelief.
"You too?"
A faint smile appeared on her lips.
Sacha pointed at him.
"See?
You’re doomed."
The elevator doors opened.
They continued through the building and eventually reached the entrance.
Outside, Sacha looked around and soon spotted a taxi approaching.
She raised her hand.
The taxi slowed and stopped near the gate.
Before getting inside, she turned toward Stan.
"Goodbye, brother..."
She paused.
Then her eyes moved toward Camilla.
A mischievous smile spread across her face.
"...and my brother’s beloved."
Camilla froze and Stan noticed immediately.
Sacha’s smile widened.
"I hope you two stay good together.
Take good care of each other, alright?"
Camilla’s cheeks immediately flushed.
She turned her face toward the side.
Sacha looked delighted.
"Bye!"
She stepped into the taxi and Stan waved at her...
"Bye, Sis."
The taxi pulled away.
Stan lowered his hand and glanced toward Camilla.
She was still looking to the side.
Her expression was unusually stiff, and the faint crimson coloring high on her cheeks had not disappeared.
Stan didn’t need enhanced senses to figure it out.
She’s blushing.
And judging from how deliberately she refused to look at him, she was probably far more embarrassed than she wanted to admit.
Stan suppressed a laugh.
Camilla finally spoke without looking at him, "Your sister is... troublesome."
Stan laughed softly.
"She likes teasing people."
Camilla remained silent for a moment.
Then she muttered, "She is too bold."
Stan looked at her with amusement, "She’s my sister."
Camilla finally glanced at him, "True."
A small smile tugged at Stan’s lips as they turned back toward the building.
Yet beneath the amusement, his thoughts returned to what he had discovered.
Sacha had comprehended Dao.
She had begun absorbing Qi.
Her cultivation path had already started, even though she didn’t know the first thing about cultivation.
And somehow, that realization felt like the beginning of something much bigger.
Stan looked toward the building ahead. ’Sis... what exactly did you comprehend?’

chapters.title: Chapter 408: Sophie's Worry
paragraphs: They watched as Sacha's taxi drove away with a soft hum...
Stan stood on the road pavement a moment longer, hands in his pockets, watching the tail lights recede. Somewhere at the corner of his mouth, was a small easy smile.

Beside him, Camilla was not smiling. She was stiff, standing with the small precise stillness of a woman who had, a few seconds ago, been called 'my brother's beloved' by a laughing twenty-two-year-old and was, in her own private assessment, still recovering.
Stan glanced at her sideways. He knew better, he could tell that her emotions were in turmoil.
But he did it anyway, he couldn't stop himself from teasing her...
"You're awfully quiet." He asked with a smile as if he didn't know why she was like this...
Camilla didn't look at him as she replied with her face still expressionless...
"I have nothing to say."
"Really?"
"Yes."
Stan smiled, "Not even about being called my belov—"
Camilla stopped walking. She turned her head very slowly. Her red eyes settled on his face with the composure of a woman who could, if she chose, remove his tongue without breaking eye contact.
"Do you want to be left on this pavement."
Stan laughed as he immediately raised both hands.
"Alright, alright. I won't mention it again."
"Wise." She resumed walking. They crossed the last stretch of the private drive in a small companionable silence.
After a few steps, quietly, almost to herself, Camilla muttered: "Your sister is troublesome."
Stan smiled. "She likes you."
Camilla's stride broke, very slightly. "...She barely knows me."
"She doesn't need long." Stan replied...
She did not answer. But he caught, in his peripheral vision, the small fractional lift at the corner of her mouth.
Stan noticed it but said nothing. 'Looks like Sis made quite a bit of progress with her.'
There had been a time when Sacha had regarded Camilla with nothing but cautious suspicion. Now she had hugged her, teased her, and even called her his beloved without hesitation.
And Camilla, despite all her usual reserve, had actually smiled back.
For some reason, the sight left a small warmth in his chest.
The doorman inclined his head.
Stan returned the nod.
Camilla's red eyes flicked toward the man for the exact length of time required to register his presence, and then away, which was, by her standards, positively cordial.
They stepped into the lobby.
Stan glanced at Camilla, "You know, you could try smiling at people more often."
"I have no reason to."
"That sounds exhausting."
"It isn't."
Stan chuckled. "Of course."
They reached the elevator. The doors opened, and the two stepped inside. As the small illuminated numbers began climbing, Camilla said, almost idly,
"She is very different from you."
"That's one way to put it."
"She is lively."
"She's always been lively."
A small pause hit them before she added,
"She is also very protective of you."
Stan's expression softened, just a little, "She means a lot to me."
He said it in the small unhurried tone of a man stating an ordinary fact. He did not elaborate.
Camilla, who had learned by now to read the shape of the sentences he chose not to finish, did not press.
After a small quiet beat, she said: "I understand why you care about her."
"Yeah."
The elevator climbed on. Stan looked at the changing numbers for a moment before adding more lightly,
"And apparently, she's now decided you're part of the family whether you agreed to it or not."
Camilla gave him a slow sideways glance. "I noticed, Stan."
Stan smiled. "She probably won't stop teasing you either."
"I don't know the mentality of you humans, but I think I understand her, at least a little."
"Good luck..."
Camilla's eyes narrowed slightly. "I don't require luck."
Stan laughed, "Right. I forgot who I was talking to."
Just as the doors opened onto his floor, his phone suddenly rang.
He looked at it and saw the person calling him was Sophie.
Stan's expression changed slightly.
He tapped answer. "Sophie?"
"Stan. Are you busy?"
"Not really. What's up?"
A small pause on the other end. That, more than anything else, caught his attention.
Sophie did not hesitate. Sophie opened conversations with verdicts.
"What happened?"
"Nothing bad."
Another small pause. "There was something I forgot to tell you before I left after visiting you... It disturbed me a lot and was one of the reasons why I decided to visit you with Maya."
Stan's brows drew together. "You forgot something?"
"Yeah." Her voice was quieter than usual.
"It was just a feeling, a premonition, premonitioms like this do happen but this was on another level, I've never felt this way before..."
He glanced sideways at Camilla. She met his eyes for a fraction of a second, immediately recognizing the change in his expression.
Then she wordlessly turned her face toward the window, giving him the courtesy of pretending very deliberately not to be listening.
Stan tapped his hand against the reader. The door clicked open. He walked inside.
"Alright," he said gently. "Tell me."
Camilla followed behind him. Sophie explained that not long after Stan had left for Antarctica, she had woken in the middle of the night.
Not from a dream or from a noise. Not from anything she could identify. Her heart had simply been hammering.
She had checked her phone. 'Nothing.'
She had checked the door. 'Locked.'
She had listened to the small ordinary sounds of Crown Jewel Tower at night, the ventilation, the faint hum of the city below, nothing unusual.

Nothing had happened around her. And yet she had been sitting up in the dark at three in the morning with her heart racing and one small, absolute, unshakeable certainty pressing against the inside of her chest.
Stan was hurt. She had not known where. She had not known how. Heck she didn't know why she was feeling this way. She had simply, unambiguously, known.
"It wasn't worry, Stan. I know what worry feels like, this isn't it."
Her voice had the small careful was a bit shaky as she tried working through the description in real time.
"It was different, like it was on another level entirely. Something inside me was telling me you were in trouble."

chapters.title: Chapter 409: Beyond Words
paragraphs: "It was different, like it was on another level entirely. Something inside me was telling me you were in trouble."
Stan went very still. In the small private back of his head, the moment settled into place with the soft, clean precision of a puzzle piece finding its slot.
He asked her the exact time she started feeling like that and upon hearing her reply, his eyes widened in surprise...
The moment she started feeling this was back when he met the four werewolves. And that despicable Elder fang or whatever he is called, who had beaten him halfway across a stretch of glacial ice.

The face-drag, the broken ribs. The specific moment somewhere in the middle of it when he had, in the small honest back of his own head, understood that he was going to die on that ice if he did not do something impossible in the next several seconds.
That time, that exact moment. He had been trying so hard to forget all about this but it all just keeps coming back...
Taking a deep breath, his eyes narrowed slightly. 'The timing matches.'
He kept his voice level. "How long did it last?"
"Hours. Then it just... stopped."
That unsettled him more than the rest of it.
"Sophie."
"Yeah?"
"Did anything happen since? Anything smaller?"
"...No. Just that one night."
A small pause hit them both at that moment, before Sophie with a voice filled with uncertainty couldn't help but ask...
"Did something happen over there, Stan?"
He hesitated, then carefully, he said in a calm voice: "Nothing you need to worry about."
A small tired exhale came from the other end.
"You always say that."
"Because it usually works."
"It doesn't."
He almost laughed, but he caught it and let it out as a slow breath instead.
"I'll tell you when I see you," he said gently. "Not on the phone."
"...Okay."
A quiet moment passed and then she said again,
"Just... be careful, okay?"
Stan's expression softened, "I will, don't worry.
"Good." They exchanged a few more words before Sophie finally said:
"Alright. I'll let you go."
"Okay. Take care."
"You too."
The line clicked off. Stan lowered his phone. For several seconds, he simply stood there.
Camilla watched him. She didn't ask immediately. She simply waited.
Finally, her calm voice broke the silence.
"That conversation troubled you."
Stan looked at her, "You noticed?"
"Yes."
A small smile appeared on his face.
"Of course you did."
Camilla didn't respond. She gave him enough space to decide whether he wanted to explain.
Eventually, Stan sighed.
"Sophie said something strange."
He gave her the shape of it. Not every word, just the important parts. The middle-of-the-night waking. The racing heart. The certainty that he was hurt somewhere far away.
And the fact that the sensation had disappeared at thesame time he healed from near death...
Camilla's expression grew noticeably more serious, "When?"
Stan met her eyes, "The time I fought Elder Fang."
Her red eyes narrowed. She said nothing for a small held moment. The significance did not require translation.

She could remember the intense craving that struck her when she saw Stan near dead with a gaping hole laying on the snow flow, Comparing the her of back then and the her of now, she seemed almost like a completely different person...
The comparison made her a bit flustered Then, in the measured tone of a woman working the problem out loud:
"Perhaps she simply sensed that something was wrong. Mortals often speak of such feelings without understanding them."
He shook his head, "She said it felt different from ordinary worry."
"And the timing was exact."
"Exact." A small silence followed.
Camilla's gaze became more focused, "You believe your connection to her permitted her to sense your condition across a distance."
Stan did not answer immediately. His silence was enough. Camilla's eyes narrowed slightly.
"That would've been possible with a Qi technique, but she's a mere mortal..."
Camilla was about to continue, when she remembered who she was talking to, she also realised that she might actually be insulting Stan's girls with her words...
She remembered last time when she called them mere insects and he told her in a time colder than he ever had that those he cared about are not insects...
Realising she might say something she would regret she fell silent and looked out through the window...
Stan was silent as well, he didn't think much of Camilla words, what bothered him most was that the system didn't tell him about this...
It told him, he could feel.their emotions and when they're in danger but didn't tell him that reverse was also the case.
It also made him wonder why his system won't come clean and tell him all that it's capable of..
He tried asking the system but all he got was silence...
Sighing, Stan walked farther into the room before sitting down on the couch.
He rested his forearms on his knees and let his hands hang loosely.
There was, quietly, a longer list forming in the back of his head than he wanted to admit.
Sacha. Her sudden ability to absorb Qi. Her unconscious resonance with Dao. The fact that she had begun awakening without even knowing the words for what was happening to her.
The system had revealed the truth only after he noticed it himself. And now Sophie.

Across thousands of kilometers, without cultivation, without spirit sense, without any obvious supernatural technique, she had awakened in the middle of the night because something inside her knew that he was being hurt.
Stan rubbed a slow hand down his face. 'First Sis begins absorbing Qi. Now Sophie can apparently sense when I'm hurt.'
His eyes narrowed. 'How many things has the system not told me?'
He wasn't afraid. Not exactly. But he was beginning to realize something important.
The system might not be the source of every supernatural phenomenon occurring around him.
It might simply be giving him access to things that already existed.
As he was deep in thought, Camilla came to stand across from him, one pale hand resting lightly on the back of the accent chair.
She did not sit or question. Instead, her hand stiffly moved to his shoulder as she said softly, "You don't need to understand it immediately."
He looked at her, he was not expecting this...
Camilla's voice remained calm.
"Not everything reveals its nature the moment it appears. Some things only become clear after enough time has passed."

chapters.title: Chapter 410: Things He Doesn’t Know
paragraphs: Stan remained silent.
She continued. "You survived. She sensed that you were in danger, and the feeling disappeared once you were safe again."
Her crimson eyes met his. "Whatever the reason, she was connected to you strongly enough to feel something she could not explain."
Stan’s expression softened slightly.
Camilla wasn’t trying to explain something she didn’t understand. She was simply giving him another way to look at it.
And strangely enough, that helped.
"Perhaps you’re right."
Camilla gave a small nod.
"You have been encountering one unusual thing after another since the return of Qi. There is no reason to expect everything to make sense immediately."
Stan let out a quiet breath. "True."
A brief silence followed. Then Camilla added:
"And if something similar happens again, you will know to pay attention."
Stan looked at her. A faint smile appeared.
"That’s actually good advice."
"I know."
He chuckled softly. But even as the conversation eased, the thought remained in the back of his mind.
Something happened between Sophie and me. He still didn’t know what.
And the fact that the system had never mentioned anything like this continued to bother him. First Sis begins absorbing Qi without even knowing what Dao is.
Now Sophie can somehow sense when I’m hurt from thousands of kilometers away.
His eyes narrowed slightly. How many things are happening around me that I haven’t noticed yet? He wasn’t afraid, not exactly.
But for the first time, Stan was beginning to suspect that the system wasn’t going to explain every mystery surrounding him.
Perhaps some answers would have to be discovered on their own. And perhaps that was exactly how it was supposed to be.
He lifted his head and grinned teasingly, "So..."
Camilla looked at him, seeing that look on his face she knew he was about to tease her, but she still asked, "What?"
"’My brother’s beloved.’" Stan grinned as he teased her by reminding her of his sister’s teasing words...
As expected, her expression stiffened instantly. "Do not."
Stan grinned. "I didn’t even finish."
"You were going to.
"...Maybe."
She gave him a flat stare.
Stan laughed in response, a small tired but genuine laugh. "Alright, alright. I’ll stop."
A beat passed, then Camilla quietly muttered: "Your sister really is troublesome."
"Yeah." Stan’s smile softened as he adde, "But I’m glad she came."
Camilla was quiet for a moment. Her red eyes softened slightly. "...So am I."
The simple answer surprised him a little. He looked at her. She didn’t elaborate. Neither did he. For a while, neither spoke.
Stan’s phone remained face down on the table. The city stretched beyond the glass, lights beginning to dominate the fading evening.
His thoughts returned to Sophie’s confession.
His eyes narrowed slightly as he thought about it, ’What else could be happening that I don’t know about?’
Camilla walked past him toward the living room. She noticed his silence but chose not to interrupt.
Stan remained seated for another moment before finally standing. The two of them continued deeper into the apartment.
For now, there were no answers, only more questions.
Stan let the silence sit for a while.
Sophie’s revelation was not going to unpack itself in one evening, and he had already spent more of the past hour in the small careful back of his own head than he had budgeted for.

Camilla was still nearby, one long pale hand resting on the arm of the accent chair, red eyes tracked idly to the sea beyond the glass, her posture had a small unhurried stillness to it... She was giving him the space to think without appearing to give him anything.
Camilla’s gaze drifted toward the kitchen.
She had been silent for several minutes, but something had been bothering her.
Or to put it more accurately, she wanted something.
Her eyes settled on the dish Stan had prepared earlier.
She hadn’t commented on it at the time, she hadn’t asked for more. She had simply eaten, as composed as ever, giving him no indication that the meal had been particularly memorable.
Yet now, only a few hours later, she found herself wanting it again. It was an unfamiliar sensation.
Camilla stood.
Stan looked up. "Where are you going?"
She didn’t answer immediately. Instead, she walked toward the kitchen and stopped near where the remaining food had been kept.
Stan watched her for a moment before understanding.
A small smile appeared on his face.
"You’re craving it."
Camilla looked over her shoulder. "I am not.
"You walked toward the food without even thinking about it."
"I was curious."
"Of course." Stan smiled...
She gave him a flat look before returning her attention to the dish.
After a moment, she glanced back at him.
"Why didn’t you mention this food earlier?"
"When?"
"When your sibling asked about what you could prepare."
Stan raised an eyebrow. "You remembered that?"
"I remember most things."
"Apparently."
She studied the dish again. "And why did you make fresh food?"
Stan’s expression changed slightly. That was a better question than she probably realized.

He considered whether to tell her. There wasn’t really any reason to hide it from her, after all, with her in his harem, she can’t really act on that info that Polar bear liver is poisonous to his sister, and with his sister becoming a Cultivator soon, she would be able to handle it... After all, she was going through the evolution stage, soon enough, she won’t be a normal human anymore...
While theres no reason to hide it from her, explaining the reason meant admitting something he hadn’t bothered mentioning earlier.
After a brief pause, he answered, "The liver."
Camilla’s eyes narrowed slightly, "The liver?"
"Yes, the liver of the beast I killed back then."
She waited.
Stan continued, "It contains a huge amount of a substance called vitamin A. Too much of it can be toxic to ordinary humans."
Camilla’s eyes flickered once. Then she understood, "I see."
She glanced toward the dish, "So that’s why."
Stan nodded. He didn’t elaborate, after all he didn’t need to.
Camilla was quiet for a moment, piecing together the implication herself. "You were being cautious with her."
"Of course. "
Her gaze returned to the food, she smiled faintly, after witnessing, Sacha and Stan sibling behaviour, with each other, their teasing and all that, she couldn’t help but imagine if Sacha knew...
"What if she saw the left overs, you would have stopped her."
"Immediately."
That earned a small amused breath from her. "You are rather protective."

"Perhaps you’re right."

"You have been encountering one unusual thing after another since the return of Qi.

"True."

"And if something similar happens again, you will know to pay attention."

Something happened between Sophie and me.

First Sis begins absorbing Qi without even knowing what Dao is.

His eyes narrowed slightly.
How many things are happening around me that I haven’t noticed yet?

"Do not."

"Alright, alright.

Camilla walked past him toward the living room.
