chapters.title: Chapter 411: A Reason To Meet
paragraphs: "What if she saw the left overs, you would have stopped her."
"Immediately."
That earned a small amused breath from her. "You are rather protective."
Stan shrugged. "Well, she’s my sister."
"I know." Camilla looked down at the dish again.
After a moment, she took another portion.
Stan watched her with a smile, "You really did like it."
Camilla ignored the comment, instead, She tasted it slowly, her expression as composed as ever.
Stan smiled, knowing she was trying hard to not let him know that she liked kt
He watched as she took another bite.
"And yet you somehow managed to make something I would want again within a few hours."
This came as a surprise, but Camilla’s calm voice made it seem off...
"That’s a complaint or a compliment?" He asked
"No." She paused and added, "A criticism of your cooking would be more difficult to justify."
Stan laughed at her dry joke, "That’s an unusually generous review."
"Don’t become arrogant."
"Too late."
She gave him a sideways look, "You are already difficult enough."
"And you’re still eating."
Camilla looked down at what she was holding. Then back at him, "I haven’t finished evaluating it."
"You’ve been evaluating it since earlier."
"I am thorough."
Stan shook his head, amused, "Right."
Camilla calmly took another bite. For once, she didn’t bother defending herself.
The quiet that followed was comfortable.
Then Stan’s phone suddenly rang. Both of their attention shifted toward the sound.
Stan reached for it and glanced at the screen. His expression shifted.
[Amelia.]
Camilla noticed the shift.
"Another one?"
"Yeah." He answered then picked the call before saying softly to the caller at the other line
"Amelia?"

"Stan." A soft, sweet feminine voice came... There was a small unfamiliar quality in her voice. Not composed. Not controlled. Something quieter and more careful than either, the small nervousness of a woman who had, apparently, been rehearsing the opening line for longer than she wanted to admit.
He noticed it.
"What’s wrong?"
"Nothing is wrong." A tiny pause echoes before her soft voice continued, "I just, wanted to ask you something."
He waited and then heard her say, "I’ve just arrived in Inksea."
Stan’s eyebrows rose. "You’re in Inksea?"
It came as a surprise cause he knew she was abroad...
"Yes." She replied...

He was, honestly, surprised. He had told her he was back only yesterday. Which meant that Amelia Don, a woman who owned significant shares in a significant film studio, who ordinarily moved with the small careful choreography of a person whose calendar was scheduled three weeks out, had, within roughly twenty-four hours of learning he had returned to Inksea, dropped whatever she had been doing on the mainland, boarded a flight, and physically transported herself to a coastal island several thousand miles from her ordinary life.
She had not waited. Not for a decent interval. Not for a plausible pretext. Not even, apparently, for the small dignity of pretending she had a reason to be in the area anyway.
Something warm settled quietly in his chest.
"I didn’t know if you’d be busy today," she continued, careful. "So I wasn’t sure whether it would be possible to meet you."
He was about to answer. She did not let him, fearing that he might cancel her out...
"I wanted to discuss something important." Her tone changed, steadier now, deliberately. "It concerns the Vanguard’s investigation."
Stan’s expression sharpened. "About Streak?"
"Yes." A small pause. "There have been developments regarding the people impersonating you and using the Streak identity. I would rather discuss it face-to-face than over the phone."

He heard it, then. Underneath the businesslike delivery. The small tight quality of a woman who had, in the split second between her question and his answer, hurried to give him areasonto say yes, because she had been afraid, in that same split second, that without one he might say no.
She had traveled here to see him.
And she had been afraid to say so.
Something in his chest turned over, quietly and without permission.
He softened his voice.
"Of course I’ll meet you."
There was a very small silence on the other end.
Then Amelia exhaled, the small released breath of a person who had been, for the last thirty seconds, unconsciously holding one.
"...Really?"
"Yeah. You came all the way to Inksea. It would be rude not to see you."
Her voice became noticeably lighter.
"Thank you."
"Send me the location."
"I will."
A pause.
"Amelia.
"Yes?"
"You didn’t have to worry about whether I’d meet you."
A quiet moment.
"...I know." Her voice was quieter now. "But I still worried."
Stan smiled faintly. "I’ll see you soon then."
"Okay."
The line clicked off.
He lowered the phone.
Camilla was looking at him with the small unhurried attention.
She was listening but had been pretending not to listen to.
"Another one who has come looking for you."
"Apparently."
"She traveled a long way because you told her you were back."
"You caught that too?"
"It was obvious."
Stan didn’t answer. But the small warmth had not left his chest, and he suspected, from the small trace of amusement in Camilla’s red eyes, that it was also not entirely invisible on his face.
"You don’t seem pleased."
"Is she another one of your harem?" She asked stiffly...
"Soon to be..." Stan replied casually...
Camilla said nothing further.
[Meanwhile, the Grand Aurelia Hotel, ninth floor.]
Amelia stood in the middle of the suite, phone still resting against her chest, staring at nothing in particular.
For several seconds, she did not move. Then, slowly, her lips pressed together.
Her eyes closed. A smile spread across her face, small and involuntary and entirely unlike the composed one she wore in boardrooms.
He had said yes. He was actually going to meet her.
Her heart, which had been running at an elevated rate since the moment she’d tapped his name, escalated by another small notch.
’I’m going to see Stan.’

She had been thinking about this moment since the flight had boarded. She had imagined it in the small idle way one imagined pleasant things during long transits, what he would say, how he would look at her, whether he would smile, whether he would notice that she had come immediately, whether that noticing would show on his face.
A small blush crept up her cheeks. ’I probably look ridiculous.’
She tried to compose herself. It did not work. Her thoughts betrayed her instantly.
’Maybe he’ll be happy to see me. Maybe he’ll ask why I came so quickly. What should I say if he does.’

chapters.title: Chapter 412: Thirty Minutes...
paragraphs: She could see it too clearly, the shape of him walking through a doorway toward her, the specific familiar cadence of his voice saying her name. Her heart thumped harder.
She covered her face with one hand.
"...Why am I this nervous."
She knew the answer. She simply did not want to say it out loud.
Because she liked him. More than she should. More than she had originally intended, back when she had been a hostile board-level executive with a low opinion of men.

Every subsequent hour spent in his company had, quietly, made the feeling harder to ignore, the trust he had extended her, the calm confidence with which he handled things that would have broken lesser men, the small persistent fact that in spite of his rise in status and reach and net worth he had never, at any point, treated her as though she were beneath him.
She smiled again, at her reflection in the tall window, and the woman in the glass smiled back.
’I’m really going to see him.’
Her eyes widened.
"...Wait."
She looked at her phone.
"I haven’t given him the address."

She opened the messaging app with the small controlled urgency of a woman refusing to acknowledge that she had almost failed a step this basic. She typed the restaurant. She hit send. She stared at the screen.
A few seconds passed.
Her phone vibrated.
[Stan: The sun will be setting soon. I’ll be there in about thirty minutes to an hour.]
Amelia froze as she read it once.
Then again, her heart, which had spent the last five minutes at an elevated rate, briefly forgot how a normal cardiac rhythm worked.
’Thirty minutes.’ She looked at the time. She looked at herself in the mirror across the room. She looked around the suite. She looked back at herself in the mirror.
"...Thirty minutes?!" Suddenly she became extremely conscious of everything. Her clothes, travel-creased. Her hair, flight-flattened on one side.
Her face, bare of the small deliberate makeup she preferred when she wanted to look as though she had not tried.

Whether she should change. Whether she should shower first. Whether she should redo her hair. Whether she should attempt to look slightly more attractive without in any visible way looking as though she had specifically prepared for him.
Her cheeks were already warm. ’He’s coming.’
Her heart thumped again. She pressed her hands against her face, "...Calm down, Amelia calm down..."
But it didn’t work, taking a deep breath, she looked at her reflection.
Looking at the beautiful reflection of herself on the mirror, she smiled, despite the nerves and everything coursing through her...
’I finally get to see him again.’
Sighing, She checked her phone, but there was no new message. Taking a deep breath, she put it down.
Ten seconds later, she picked it up again...
’Still nothing.’ Realising her current condition, she laughed quietly at herself. "...I’m hopeless."
Then she got to work.
[Back at Aurelia Heights.]
Stan pocketed his phone. Camilla watched him with the same quiet, unhurried attention she had maintained for most of the past hour.
For a moment, neither said anything.
Then, all of a sudden, Camilla spoke, "The game."
Stan glanced at her. "What about it?"
He was slightly confused. They had already finished playing Uno some time ago. He hadn’t expected her to bring it up again now, especially when he was preparing to leave.
Camilla seemed to notice his confusion, "It was good."
Stan blinked, "Uno?"
She nodded. "Yes, I found it... interesting."
A faint smile touched Stan’s lips. "You actually enjoyed it."
"I didn’t say that."
"You didn’t have to."
Camilla ignored him and went on, "It made me curious about the other games new age humans play."
Stan’s eyebrows lifted. "Other games?"
"Yes." She paused, apparently considering how to phrase it. "If you can obtain more of them, I’d like you to bring some back."
Stan looked at her for a second. "You want me to buy you games?"
"Is that difficult?"
"Not remotely."
"Then there is no problem."
He chuckled. "What kind?"
"I don’t know." Camilla glanced toward the table where the Uno cards still lay.
"Something that requires thought would be preferable."
"Strategy games?"
"Perhaps."
"Something competitive?"
"Obviously."
Stan smiled. "Of course."
"And not everything needs to involve fighting."
That caught him slightly off guard. "That’s a surprisingly important qualification."
"I have spent enough time fighting."
Stan nodded. "Fair."
Camilla looked at him again, "Find some good ones."
"How many?
She considered it. "A reasonable number."
"That’s not a number."
"It is sufficient."
Stan laughed. "You really don’t want to make this easy for me."
"I assumed you were capable of choosing."
"I am."
He glanced at the clock. "Fine. I’ll find you some."
Camilla gave a small nod. "Good."
Stan reached toward the counter and picked up his keys. As he slipped them into his hand, Camilla added calmly,
"And perhaps bring another game like the one we played."
Stan looked back at her. "I thought you wanted something different."
"I said perhaps."
A faint smile appeared on her lips. "I never said I disliked that one."
’You never said you disliked it but you don’t want to admit that you like it...’ Stan shook his head with a smile, amused. "Got it."
He pocketed his keys. "I’ll see what I can find."

With that, he checked his phone once more, the location was already saved. Camilla watched him move through the small ordinary choreography of a man preparing to leave his own home in the early evening.
"Will you be gone long?"
"Probably not."
"You intend to return tonight?"
"Of course."
A brief pause.
"You’re staying here?" Stan asked her...
"For now."
"Alright." Sighing, he started toward the door. But then stopped and turned around, not forgetting to tease her...
"Don’t destroy anything while I’m gone."
Camilla gave him an entirely offended look. "I have never destroyed anything unnecessarily."
"That’s a very specific defense."
"I am simply stating a fact." She replied calmly...
Stan laughed and pulled the door shut behind him.

Looking at the beautiful reflection of herself on the mirror, she smiled, despite the nerves and everything coursing through her...
’I finally get to see him again.’
Sighing, She checked her phone, but there was no new message.
Taking a deep breath, she put it down.
Ten seconds later, she picked it up again...
’Still nothing.’ Realising her current condition, she laughed quietly at herself.
"...I’m hopeless."
Then she got to work.
[Back at Aurelia Heights.]
Stan pocketed his phone.
Camilla watched him with the same quiet, unhurried attention she had maintained for most of the past hour.
For a moment, neither said anything.
Then, all of a sudden, Camilla spoke, "The game."
Stan glanced at her.
"What about it?"
He was slightly confused.
They had already finished playing Uno some time ago.
He hadn’t expected her to bring it up again now, especially when he was preparing to leave.
Camilla seemed to notice his confusion, "It was good."
Stan blinked, "Uno?"
She nodded.
"Yes, I found it... interesting."
A faint smile touched Stan’s lips.
"You actually enjoyed it."
"I didn’t say that."
"You didn’t have to."
Camilla ignored him and went on, "It made me curious about the other games new age humans play."
Stan’s eyebrows lifted.
"Other games?"
"Yes." She paused, apparently considering how to phrase it.
"If you can obtain more of them, I’d like you to bring some back."
Stan looked at her for a second.
"You want me to buy you games?"
"Is that difficult?"
"Not remotely."
"Then there is no problem."
He chuckled.
"What kind?"
"I don’t know." Camilla glanced toward the table where the Uno cards still lay.
"Something that requires thought would be preferable."
"Strategy games?"
"Perhaps."
"Something competitive?"
"Obviously."
Stan smiled.
"Of course."
"And not everything needs to involve fighting."
That caught him slightly off guard.
"That’s a surprisingly important qualification."
"I have spent enough time fighting."
Stan nodded.
"Fair."
Camilla looked at him again, "Find some good ones."
"How many?
She considered it.
"A reasonable number."
"That’s not a number."
"It is sufficient."
Stan laughed.
"You really don’t want to make this easy for me."
"I assumed you were capable of choosing."
"I am."
He glanced at the clock.
"Fine.
I’ll find you some."
Camilla gave a small nod.
"Good."
Stan reached toward the counter and picked up his keys.
As he slipped them into his hand, Camilla added calmly,
"And perhaps bring another game like the one we played."
Stan looked back at her.
"I thought you wanted something different."
"I said perhaps."
A faint smile appeared on her lips.
"I never said I disliked that one."
’You never said you disliked it but you don’t want to admit that you like it...’ Stan shook his head with a smile, amused.
"Got it."
He pocketed his keys.
"I’ll see what I can find."
With that, he checked his phone once more, the location was already saved.
Camilla watched him move through the small ordinary choreography of a man preparing to leave his own home in the early evening.
"Will you be gone long?"
"Probably not."
"You intend to return tonight?"
"Of course."
A brief pause.
"You’re staying here?" Stan asked her...
"For now."
"Alright." Sighing, he started toward the door.
But then stopped and turned around, not forgetting to tease her...
"Don’t destroy anything while I’m gone."
Camilla gave him an entirely offended look.
"I have never destroyed anything unnecessarily."
"That’s a very specific defense."
"I am simply stating a fact." She replied calmly...
Stan laughed and pulled the door shut behind him.

chapters.title: Chapter 413: A Small Detour...
paragraphs: Closing the door behind him, Stan casually walked to the elevator and got inside...

The elevator was empty. He watched the numbers count downward and, in the small quiet that always seemed to gather inside a descending elevator, permitted his thoughts to move for a moment across the shape of the day.
Sacha, in the past two days, drifting into small unfocused inward looks he had told himself were tiredness.
Sophie, three thousand miles away, sitting up in the dark at three in the morning because her body had known his was on fire.

Amelia, boarding a flight within twenty-four hours of learning he was back, arriving in Inksea, and, with the small careful hurry of a woman who had been afraid the answer might be no, asking to see him.
Three different people. Three different developments. His life, quietly, complicating itself along multiple lines at once.
He found, to his mild surprise, that he did not dislike it.
There was something warm about being wanted.
He smiled faintly. ’I suppose I’m not completely alone anymore.’
The doors opened onto the lobby.
The doorman inclined his head. Stan returned the nod and walked out into the fading gold of the late afternoon, down the small private drive toward the parking area at the side of the building.
The Lamborghini waited in its slot, catching the low sun in long liquid streaks along its dark paint.
He unlocked it. The car answered with the soft mechanical click of a vehicle that had been designed by people who thought a lot about what a door should sound like.
He slid into the driver’s seat. Before starting the engine, he looked, one more time, at Amelia’s message.

’I finally get to see him again’ would not have shown up in the text. The text was a hotel and a suite number and nothing else. But Stan, in the small quiet of his parked car, could hear it under the letters just the same.
He smiled.
"Alright."
The engine came alive with the low unhurried growl of an aggressively expensive piece of Italian engineering, and the Lamborghini pulled smoothly out of the private drive.
The sun was beginning its slow descent toward the horizon.
The coastal road unspooled ahead of him in long warm bars.

At the other end of it, in a hotel suite nine floors above the promenade, a woman he had not intended to matter this much to him was standing in front of a mirror trying, and failing, to compose her heart.
Stan pressed the accelerator down, easy and unhurried.
The Lamborghini moved smoothly along the coastal road, its engine a subdued growl beneath the fading sounds of the city.
Stan drove with one hand resting comfortably on the wheel, the other occasionally shifting gears as the road opened ahead of him.
His thoughts, however, had already drifted away from the road.
Camilla. More specifically, Camilla pretending she didn’t like Uno.
He smiled.
She had maintained that same composed expression throughout the conversation, as though requesting more games was nothing more than a practical decision.
’I never said I disliked that one.’
Stan almost laughed again. "Right."
She had been trying remarkably hard not to admit that she enjoyed it. And somehow, that had made the whole thing more amusing.
He glanced at the road ahead. If he was being honest, he hadn’t expected Camilla to take an interest in something as mundane as a card game.
She was a vampire and a Cultivator that have probably seen many things... Yet somehow, Uno had managed to catch her attention.
Stan shook his head with a faint smile. "Maybe I should’ve introduced her to modern entertainment sooner."
He had actually been considering it. Games consoles, modern video games. Perhaps even some multiplayer games he could play with her.
But that could wait. For now, she had specifically asked for games she could use to pass the time, and he had promised to find her some. Uno was obvious. Chess was another.
A game based on strategy, prediction, positioning, and reading an opponent’s intentions.
Camilla would probably enjoy that. Beyond those two, though, he couldn’t immediately think of anything else that would suit her.
There were plenty of modern strategy games, but most required some kind of device.
He’d introduce her to those later. For now, cards and chess would do. His eyes wandered briefly toward the storefronts passing by.
Then one particular sign caught his attention. Stan slowed.
A small game and hobby shop sat along the roadside, its front window displaying board games, playing cards, puzzles, and various other items.
His eyes lingered on the display. He glanced toward the road ahead. Then back at the shop.
"...Worth a look."
He indicated, turned into the small parking area, and brought the Lamborghini to a smooth stop.
The contrast between the expensive sports car and the modest little shop was almost comical.
Stan stepped out, locked the vehicle, and walked toward the entrance.
The bell above the door gave a soft chime as he entered.
"Welcome!" A young woman behind the counter looked up with a practiced smile.
Then her expression changed. Her eyes widened.
She stared at him for a second as a soft shocked voice came out the next second, "...Wait."
Stan stopped with a bit of surprise by the sudden unexpected outburst... He could only watch as the woman’s mouth fell slightly open. "You’re..."
She immediately straightened and added, "Student Tycoon Stan?"
Stan gave her a polite smile. "Yeah."
Her face lit up, "Oh my God."
She quickly stepped out from behind the counter, "I’m a huge fan of yours!"
Stan blinked.
The enthusiasm was genuine. She seemed almost embarrassed by how excited she had become.
"I’m sorry," she said quickly. "I just, it’s really surprising to see you here. I never imagined someone like you would actually come into a shop like this."
Stan gave a small laugh, "I’m still a customer."
"Of course!" She nodded rapidly. "Of course. I’m sorry."

chapters.title: Chapter 414: Someone Special
paragraphs: "Of course!" She nodded rapidly. "Of course. I'm sorry."
She looked toward the Lamborghini visible through the glass storefront, then back at him.
"It's just... you're Student Tycoon Stan."
Stan maintained the polite smile. 'While my game video has gone viral and risen to unimaginable levels over the past few weeks, I've apparently already developed a fan base.'
He wasn't quite sure how he felt about that. It was flattering, mostly. But there was something strange about suddenly being recognized everywhere.
A few weeks ago, he could walk through places without anyone caring.
Now, apparently, even a small hobby shop had someone who knew his name.
'I don't know whether I should be pleased or worried.'
The woman seemed to recover her composure.
"Is there anything you're looking for?"
"Actually, yes." Stan glanced around the shelves.
"Do you have Uno?"
"Uno?"
She brightened. "Absolutely."
She immediately walked toward one of the shelves. "We have several versions."
She pulled out a few boxes. "Classic Uno, Uno Flip, and a couple of themed editions."
Stan looked them over.
"Classic."
He picked it up. "Do you have chess?"
"Yes."
She led him to another section.
"We have several boards. Wooden ones, travel sets, magnetic sets..."
Stan examined them briefly before choosing a simple wooden set. Nothing excessively ornate. Just a proper chessboard with well-made pieces.
He held it up. "This one."
"Good choice." She carried both items toward the counter. Stan followed.
As she scanned them, she glanced at him again.
"Are these for you?"
"No."
She smiled. "A gift?"
"Something like that." He could already imagine Camilla sitting across from him, studying the chessboard like it was a battlefield.
Then, eventually, insisting that she had merely been evaluating it. The thought made him smile.
The attendant noticed. "Someone special?
Stan looked at her. There was a brief pause. Then he smiled politely, "Just someone who asked for them."
The woman nodded, wisely deciding not to pry. She finished the transaction and gave him the total.
Stan paid without hesitation. As she handed him the bag, he glanced around the shop once more.
It was small, but surprisingly well stocked.
"You've got a nice place."
The woman's expression brightened again. "Thank you."
She looked genuinely pleased by the compliment.
Stan reached into his wallet and placed a little extra cash on the counter.
She stared at it. "Sir?"
"For the help."
Her eyes widened. "Oh, no, you don't have to..."
"It's fine."
She hesitated before accepting it. "Thank you. Really."
Stan nodded. "Have a good evening."
"You too."
He turned toward the door.
Then she called after him. "Stan!"
He looked back and then she smiled waving at him, "Good luck."
Stan raised an eyebrow. "With what?"
She laughed awkwardly. "I don't know. Whatever you're doing."
He smiled. "Thanks."
The bell chimed again as he stepped outside. The evening air greeted him.
Stan walked back toward the Lamborghini with the small shopping bag in hand.
He glanced down at it. 'Uno. Chess. That should be enough for now.'
He could already imagine Camilla's expression when he returned. Probably that same carefully neutral look. Probably followed by some variation of I was merely curious.
Stan laughed quietly. "Yeah. We'll see about that."
He placed the games in the passenger seat, closed the door, and slid back behind the wheel.
The engine came alive. Stan pulled out of the parking lot and merged back onto the coastal road.
His destination hadn't changed. Amelia was waiting. But now he had one more small reason to look forward to returning home afterward.
The Lamborghini moved through Inksea in the small unhurried speed
The sun had begun its slow decline. The coastal light was going from gold into the softer amber of early evening.

The city was beginning to light up along its lower edges, the small warm-lit shopfronts along the promenade, the traffic signals cycling through their patient rotations, the pale blue-white glow of the taller buildings starting to catch against the darkening sky.
Stan drove with one hand on the wheel and his thoughts loose.

Sacha's awakening. Sophie, three thousand miles away, waking in the dark with her heart racing because her body had known his was on fire. Amelia, boarding a flight within twenty-four hours of learning he was back.
Three developments. Three separate lines. All moving in the same general direction, all moving faster than he had budgeted for.
He shook his head, faintly.
'Things really have become interesting lately.'

Eventually, the restaurant Amelia had chosen resolved out of the coastal skyline, a low, elegant, well-lit building along the promenade with tall shaped hedges along its street frontage and the small quiet exterior of a place that catered exclusively to people who preferred not to be overheard. Comfortable without being ostentatious. Private without being conspicuously so.
Amelia's taste. Stan pulled into the discreet parking area, killed the engine, stepped out.
Before walking in, he drew his phone from his pocket and typed a single line.
[Stan: I'm here.]
He hit send. Then he pocketed the phone and walked toward the entrance.
Inside the restaurant, Amelia had been seated in the corner for the better part of an hour.

She had, in that time, checked her phone approximately four times more than the small dignity of a grown woman would have preferred. She had straightened the collar of her blouse twice. She had, at one point, deliberately turned her phone face-down so that she would stop checking it, and had then, precisely eleven seconds later, turned it face-up again on the grounds that a message might come in that she would need to see immediately.
She had, in her own private assessment, been being ridiculous.
She had also, in her own private assessment, been entirely unable to stop.
The phone lit up.
[Stan: I'm here.]
Her heart gave one small unfair leap.
[He's here.]

Her fingers, which had been resting composedly around the stem of her water glass a moment before, moved with the small quick unconscious efficiency of a woman who was trying very hard not to look as though she was moving quickly.
[Amelia: I'm inside. Corner table on the left.]
And then she sent it. Then she reached, almost without thinking, to smooth the front of her blouse.
Then to adjust the fall of her hair over one shoulder.
Then, catching herself in the small polished reflection of the water glass in front of her, she drew a slow careful breath.
'Calm down.'
'It's just Stan.'
A small pause.
'...It's Stan... he isn't just anybody...'
That did not help. Her heart accelerated by another small unhelpful notch.

chapters.title: Chapter 415: Between The Lines
paragraphs: He came in. She saw him the moment he crossed the threshold.

The restaurant's warm lamplight caught along his shoulders as he moved through the low-lit room. She watched him scan the space in the small unhurried way a man scanned a room he had been given directions to. His eyes found her almost immediately.
He started toward her.

And Amelia, Amelia Don, who had spent the past several years being the most collected person in every room she walked into, who could hold a boardroom to attention with a raised eyebrow, who had, only around a week ago, been the woman who had authorized a Vanguard maritime team on a hunch, sat in her corner table and watched him walk across the restaurant, and did not, in any honest sense, look away.
She took him in. The easy confident line of the way he moved. The small calm quality of his expression.

The subtle sharpening that had, in the several days since she'd last seen him in person, settled somewhere along his features, his skin cleaner, his shoulders squarer, the small quiet gravity of him more pronounced.
He looked, she thought, like a man who had recently done something serious and come back on the other side of it.
Her heart gave another involuntary thump. 'He's even more handsome than I remember.'
She caught herself. 'Stop staring.'

She could not, entirely, stop staring. She watched him reach the table. Watched him pull out the chair opposite hers. Watched him sit down with the small easy grace of a man arriving at an ordinary dinner.
Only then did she realize that she had, in fact, been staring for slightly longer than was consistent with the small careful dignity she had been intending to project.
She looked down. Stan noticed the small shift in her expression.
He did not comment.
He smiled, the small easy relaxed smile that had, on more than one occasion in the past several weeks, done unfair things to her cardiac rhythm.
"How are you doing?"
"I'm doing well."
He studied her for a beat. "You look tired."
"I just flew here."
"That explains it."
A small smile lifted the corner of her mouth despite herself.
"You're the one who made me come all this way.
Stan raised an eyebrow. "I only told you I was back."
"You knew I'd come."
"I didn't."
She gave him a look. "...Really."
He laughed, a small warm laugh that undid the last of her professional composure by a small unhelpful degree.
"Alright. Maybe I suspected."
That made her smile.
The small nervous tightness she had been carrying since he had walked in eased, one shade.
They did not, at first, discuss any of what she had come to discuss.

Stan asked about her work. She asked about his time away. They circled through the small pleasant ordinary topics. After all they've not seen one another in person for sometime and because they like one another's company, they ended up the long way into the actual business.
She lightly complained about how much had accumulated on her desk over the past ten days.
He teased her about working too much.
She countered that someone had to keep track of the small ongoing catastrophes he apparently could not stop generating.
He laughed. She, quietly, noticed that she was enjoying herself.
Not the meeting. Not the intelligence. Not the small serious business she had flown across the country to raise with him.

Just, this. Being across from him. Talking to him without any of the small careful choreography of a scheduled encounter. Watching his hands rest lightly on the table. Watching his face when he listened to her. Watching the small unhurried focus he gave to whatever she happened to be saying at the moment she was saying it.
'I missed this.'
She subtly watched him whenever he was not looking at her.
His hands. His mouth. The small easy grace with which he lifted his water glass. The small crease at the corner of his eye when she said something that amused him.
Every small ordinary observation made the thing she had been quietly not-saying to herself, for weeks now, harder to keep unsaid.
Eventually, the conversation slowed.
Amelia took a small careful sip of her drink. Her expression settled into the more professional line she wore in boardrooms.
"Well apart from the Streak case, there was another reason I wanted to meet you."
Stan looked at her. "Yes, what's that?"
She set her glass down. "My network picked up something unusual over the past several days."
He became attentive. "Go on."

She gave it to him plainly. Tremors in international intelligence traffic. Several governments quietly redirecting personnel and material toward polar research. A notable spike in encrypted communications. Research groups that ordinarily operated independently suddenly beginning to communicate with one another. Fragments of intercepted traffic that made repeated reference to an "Antarctic incident."
She watched him as she spoke. Not as a briefer.
After all she suspected the small serious thing she was reporting on and the man sitting across from her were more closely connected than either of them was going to admit at this table.
"I thought you might be interested." Her tone was careful. "You were in Antarctica recently."
Stan's expression did not change. "Governments investigate strange things all the time."
She studied his face. "You don't think it's connected."
He gave a small, mild shrug. "Maybe. Maybe not." A beat. "I wouldn't worry about it yet."
She did not, entirely, believe him.
But she had learned, over the small careful time of getting to know him, that when Stan did not want to discuss something, pressure accomplished nothing.
He simply, quietly, moved around it, and the person doing the pressuring ended up talking to the outside of a very polite wall.
She nodded. "Alright."
Internally, she thought: 'He's hiding something.'
She did not know what. Strangely, she found that she was, increasingly, over time, one of the things she liked about him.

chapters.title: Chapter 416: Do You Like Me?
paragraphs: Internally, she thought: ’He’s hiding something.’
She did not know what. Strangely, she found that she was, increasingly, over time, one of the things she liked about him.
Taking a deep breath, She shifted the conversation. "There’s more."
"Go."
"The Streak situation has developed."
His expression sharpened one degree. "The Vanguard has rolled up two more copycat operations in the last four days."

She laid it out for him. The additional networks impersonating him. The fact that these were not random scammers, they were organized, well-funded, and clearly working from a shared playbook. The uncomfortable observation that they appeared to have access to information about the real Streak that ought not to have been public. She suspected Tiktuk platform itself might have a hand in this...

They were not merely exploiting the name. They were using his reputation to build networks, attract wealthy targets, and establish credibility across several apparently unrelated schemes. The Vanguard was now, cautiously, developing the working theory that a single larger syndicate was operating beneath at least four of the fronts they’d identified so far.
Stan listened. "Do they know who’s behind it."
"Not yet."
"Von?"
"We’re still squeezing what we have out of what we already have. He’s a piece. He’s not the whole picture."
"How close are you?"
"Closer than we were." She permitted herself a small smile. "But not close."
Stan nodded slowly. "Good."
She watched him. "You’re not surprised."
"I expected there’d be more behind it."
Her eyebrow arched. "You did?"
"People don’t build something that large off a single scam. Something that reaches has been assembling itself for longer than the scam that broke it into the open."
She smiled, small and pleased. "That’s why I wanted to tell you in person."
He gave her a small knowing look. "You’re getting better at this."
"At what."
"Reading situations."
Her smile widened, small and pleased and proud.
"I’ll take that as a compliment."
"It was."
Once the small serious business had been laid down between them, the atmosphere at the table eased again.
Amelia leaned back in her chair, drink in hand, and permitted a small playful comment.
"You know," she said, "most people come back from a trip and tell their friends about the food they ate."
Stan raised an eyebrow. "And?"
"You come back from Antarctica and somehow have several governments scrambling.
He laughed, he could tell she was teasing, but she was unbelievably bad with her jokes, maybe it was because she was nervous, since he can sense her nervousness..
"That’s not my fault."
"Don’t worry I trust you," She shook her head as she added, "But you’re impossible."
"And yet you flew to Inksea."
The words slipped out easily. They did not stay easy for long.
Amelia froze for half a second.
Stan noticed.
She looked, very quickly, down at her drink. "I had work."
"You could have handled it remotely."
"I needed to discuss it in person."
"Convenient."
She looked back at him. Her eyes were, she was well aware, a small unhelpful shade warmer than she had intended.
"Are you teasing me."
"Maybe."
She smiled, small and a little unsteady. "Then perhaps I should stop giving you opportunities."
Stan leaned back slightly in his chair. "You probably should."
The conversation drifted on.
But as it did, Stan, who had spent the last several minutes smiling at the small unguarded moments Amelia had let slip past her usual careful exteri
She looked at him for slightly longer than the conversation required.
She smiled more easily than she did around other people. He had seen her with other people. This was a different expression.
She seemed, in a small unadvertised way, genuinely happy to be sitting across from him.
She had flown to Inksea within a day of learning he was back. She had booked a hotel suite.

She had spent, he suspected, with a small quiet certainty he could not have justified in a court of law but was entirely sure of nonetheless, the last three quarters of an hour before he arrived rehearsing.
He decided he shouldn’t keep her waiting...
Sighing inwardly, he watched her, quietly, over the rim of his glass. ’Its time I make my move since she’s so scared that I would reject her that she doesn’t want to speak her mind...’
As he thought this, he stared intently at her for far too long
Amelia felt the weight of it, eventually, and looked up.
"What.
"Nothing."
"Why are you looking at me like that."
He smiled. "Just thinking."
"About what."
He did not answer immediately.
He studied her face.

She became, visibly, without meaning to, increasingly self-conscious. The small pale warmth along her cheeks that had faded during the professional stretch of the conversation returned, one shade. Her fingers, resting composedly around the stem of her glass a moment before, tightened by a very small fraction.
She was not going to be the one to look away first.
She had, however, no idea what to do with the small careful attention he was giving her.
Stan set his glass down. He decided, in the small easy back of his head, that subtlety was not going to move this any further tonight.
He gave her a small unhurried smile.
"Amelia."
"Be honest with me."
She straightened slightly. "What?"
He looked directly into her eyes.
"Do you like me."
Silence. Amelia froze.

Her heart, which had, over the course of the past hour, worked its way from an elevated baseline into a steady controlled hammering. Some small internal instrument, somewhere in the base of her chest, registered the question and produced a small alarmed ping that echoed nowhere anyone could hear.
She had been ready for many things at this table. She had not, not remotely, been ready for that.
Stan simply watched her with a calm, curious smile
Her mind went blank.

The woman who could, without missing a beat, brief a board of directors on the movements of a criminal syndicate across four national jurisdictions found, at that specific moment, that she was entirely unable to produce a single useful English sentence.
Her lips parted, very slightly.
The small pale warmth along her cheeks deepened into something rather more visible.
Her heart, which had briefly stopped, resumed at a rate that would have concerned a physician.
She stared at him and he stared back.
Neither of them spoke for a second. The small warm light of the restaurant went quietly on around them.
Outside the window, along the promenade, the last of the evening’s gold slipped over the horizon into blue.
And Amelia Don, composed executive, seasoned strategist, quietly infatuated woman, sat frozen across from Stan Harrison, and did not, for one very long silent moment, know what to say.

chapters.title: Chapter 417: You’re Thinking Too Much
paragraphs: For several seconds, Amelia simply stared at him.
The question kept replaying in her head, the way certain sentences do when a person is not entirely sure they have really been said.
’Do you like me.’
Her heart was pounding hard enough she could almost hear it.

She had imagined this moment before. More times than she would ever admit. But never like this. In every version she had rehearsed, she had been the one gathering the courage. Every version had involved her carefully choosing a time, a place, a form of words, and then, depending on the day, either confessing, or being rejected, or watching him smile and change the subject, or, on the coward days, saying nothing at all.
She had never once, in any of those versions, imagined him asking first.
Her fingers tightened, slightly, around her glass.
’Is this really happening.’
She looked at him again, Stan was not laughing. He was not teasing. His expression was calm, but his eyes were serious.
He was actually waiting for an answer.
She looked down at her drink. Her face was beginning, unmistakably, to warm.
’He asked me.’ The realization felt almost unreal. ’He actually asked me.’

For what felt like an eternity since he saved her, she had wondered whether the feeling she had been quietly carrying was entirely one-sided. He had been kind to her. He had trusted her. He had sought her out. He had listened. None of those things necessarily meant what she wanted them to mean.
And now, without warning, he had asked her directly.
A small, almost disbelieving smile threatened at the corner of her mouth.
’It’s happening. I didn’t even have to ask him.’ Her rational side, ever punctual, intervened. ’Don’t get ahead of yourself.’

Because, and she made herself sit with the thought properly, asking whether she liked him was not the same as saying he liked her. He might simply have noticed her behavior. He might simply be curious. He might, in his own way, be trying to understand what he was looking at.
There were countless explanations. She quietly scolded herself. ’Don’t be stupid, Amelia. He hasn’t said anything yet.’

Stan watched her, quietly. He could see the small conflict crossing her face. The way her eyes moved. The way her fingers had shifted, twice, on the stem of her glass. The way the pale warmth along her cheeks had gone from a shade to a full soft flush.

For once, the woman who could hold perfect composure through a briefing on international criminal syndicates was, at his corner table in an Inksea restaurant, entirely unsure what to do with her own hands.
His expression softened. He did not press. He simply waited.
After several long seconds, Amelia drew a small careful breath.
Her voice, when it came, was quieter than usual.
"Yes."
Stan remained silent, he smiled as she still did not look at him, probably too shy confessing her feelings...
"Yes," she said again, almost as though saying it a second time made the confession more real.
"I do."
There was a small held silence between them.
Then, softly: "I like you."
A tiny pause.
"More than I probably should."

She gave a small nervous laugh, the kind of laugh a person produced when they had, in the last four seconds, done something they had spent months not doing, and were now trying to acclimate to the sudden strange fact of the world having not ended.
"I’ve known for a while."
Then, finally, she looked at him. Her eyes were a mixture of embarrassment and relief and a small unguarded happiness she was not entirely successful at hiding.
"I just didn’t know if I should say anything."

Something loosened in her chest. For so long she had carried the feeling quietly. She had found small ordinary excuses to see him. She had looked forward to his messages. She had worried when he had disappeared. She had flown to Inksea almost the moment she had learned he was back, and had told herself, every time, that there had been a practical reason. Work. Information. Business. The Vanguard. Streak. Anything other than the obvious.
Now she had said it. And, strangely, she felt lighter.
’I actually said it.’
She almost wanted to laugh. She almost wanted to cry. Not from sadness. From relief.
She had spent so many small quiet nights wondering what would happen if he ever found out.
Now he knew. And she was still sitting there. He had not walked away. The world had not ended.
Then, unbidden, the next thought arrived.
She glanced up at him. Cautiously.
’But what does this mean.’
Her heart sank, one small unwelcome inch.
’He asked if I liked him. He never said that he liked me.’

She realized, with the small quick embarrassment of a woman who had permitted herself to hope, that she may have unconsciously read his question as an admission. And it was not necessarily one. Perhaps he had only wanted confirmation. Perhaps he had noticed her behavior and wanted to settle his curiosity. Perhaps he did not feel the same way, and had simply, kindly, in his careful Stan way, wanted to give her space to say it before things drifted any further.
Her fingers tightened, again, around the stem of her glass.
She looked away. The warmth along her cheeks remained, but there was, now, a small uncertain edge beneath it.
Stan noticed the shift immediately. A moment ago, she had looked relieved.
Now she was pulling small careful walls back up around herself.
He understood why. She had answered his question. He had not answered hers.
He smiled, faintly. "Amelia."
She looked up. "Yes?"
"You’re thinking too much."
Her eyes widened, slightly. "How do you know."
"Because I’ve been watching you."
That did not help her small unsteady composure at all. She looked back down at her drink.
Stan let out a quiet laugh.
What do you guys think of the story so far?

He had not walked away.
The world had not ended.
Then, unbidden, the next thought arrived.
She glanced up at him.
Cautiously.
’But what does this mean.’
Her heart sank, one small unwelcome inch.
’He asked if I liked him.
He never said that he liked me.’
She realized, with the small quick embarrassment of a woman who had permitted herself to hope, that she may have unconsciously read his question as an admission.
And it was not necessarily one.
Perhaps he had only wanted confirmation.
Perhaps he had noticed her behavior and wanted to settle his curiosity.
Perhaps he did not feel the same way, and had simply, kindly, in his careful Stan way, wanted to give her space to say it before things drifted any further.
Her fingers tightened, again, around the stem of her glass.
She looked away.
The warmth along her cheeks remained, but there was, now, a small uncertain edge beneath it.
Stan noticed the shift immediately.
A moment ago, she had looked relieved.
Now she was pulling small careful walls back up around herself.
He understood why.
She had answered his question.
He had not answered hers.
He smiled, faintly.
"Amelia."
She looked up.
"Yes?"
"You’re thinking too much."
Her eyes widened, slightly.
"How do you know."
"Because I’ve been watching you."
That did not help her small unsteady composure at all.
She looked back down at her drink.
Stan let out a quiet laugh.

chapters.title: Chapter 418: Not One Sided
paragraphs: "You're thinking too much."
"How do you know."
"Because I've been watching you." Stan laughed...
Amelia's heart, which had spent the past several minutes beating far too hard, briefly forgot how to operate at all.
She stared at him.

The soft amber glow of the table lamp caught the quiet certainty in his eyes. Around them the restaurant continued its low, unhurried rhythm, the muted clink of glassware, the distant murmur of a couple two tables over, the faint brush of a server's sleeve as someone passed behind her chair. None of it registered. There was only the man across from her and the words he had just spoken.
"What... does that mean?"
Stan's smile was small, almost private. "It means you're not the only one who feels this way."

He let the silence breathe. He did not rush to fill it. He simply watched her with the calm, unhurried attention of a man who had finally said something he had been quietly not-saying for longer than he had realized. The warmth of the lamplight rested against the side of his face.
Outside the tall windows, the city lights of Inksea shimmered along the darkening promenade, soft gold and white reflected in long, liquid streaks against the glass.
"I've noticed the way you look at me."

Amelia went, instantly, another shade warmer. Heat bloomed across her cheeks, sudden and impossible to hide. She could feel it beneath her skin, the tell-tale flush that always betrayed her when she least wanted it to.
"...You noticed."
"For a while."
She very much wanted to disappear into the water glass. The cool condensation on its surface pressed against her fingertips when she shifted them slightly. Stan's smile deepened, quiet and knowing.
"And I noticed how quickly you came to Inksea after you found out I was back."
She looked down at the linen tablecloth, smooth and pale beneath her hands. "That was work."
"Of course."
She gave him a small, suspicious sideways look. The corner of his mouth curved further. "You don't believe me."
"Not even a little."
A soft, almost unwilling laugh escaped her, low enough that it barely carried past their table. His expression softened then, the teasing light in his eyes giving way to something quieter.
"But honestly, Amelia, I was glad you came."
That landed on her with more weight than a longer declaration would have.
Because she understood, at once, that he was not saying it as a compliment. He was saying it as a fact.

The words settled into the space between them, warm and solid, and for a moment she could only sit with the quiet truth of them. The faint scent of his cologne, clean, understated, with a trace of something woody, reached her when he shifted slightly in his chair.
"I asked," he continued, voice low, "because I wanted to know if what I was feeling wasn't one-sided."
Amelia's eyes widened. Her pulse stuttered once, hard, against her throat.
He smiled. "I like you too."
The restaurant was still going quietly on around them.

The small warm lamplight. The low murmur of conversation. The soft brush of fabric as a server passed behind her chair. The city lights along the promenade catching against the darkening windows. None of it, for a second, mattered.
There were only four words.
'I like you too.'

He liked her. The man she had quietly fallen for. The man she had privately convinced herself she might never actually be able to confess to. The man whose attention she treasured far more than she should. He liked her. And she had not even had to risk the rejection first.

A tiny smile began to form at the corners of her mouth. She looked down, because she did not know how to contain it. The cool rim of her glass brushed her knuckles as she pressed her lips together, trying to suppress the expression.
It did not work.
Stan noticed. "Why are you smiling?"
"I'm not."
"You are."
"I'm not."
"You definitely are."
She finally looked up at him. The soft light caught the quiet amusement in his eyes, the faint crease at the corner of his mouth. "Don't ruin it."
Stan laughed softly, low, warm, the sound carrying only as far as their table.
They sat with it for a moment.

The quiet between them felt different now. Easier. Charged, but no longer careful. Amelia could feel the residual heat in her face, the steady thrum of her pulse still elevated, the cool air from a nearby vent brushing lightly across the back of her neck. Then, quietly, she said:
"I thought I was being obvious."
He smiled. "You were."
Her eyes widened again. "And you knew."
"I suspected."
"You suspected."
"Enough to ask."
She shook her head, a small, rueful sound escaping her. "You're terrible."
"Maybe."
She smiled, small and a little softer now. "Then why didn't you say anything sooner?"
Stan considered the question, his gaze remaining steady on hers. "I wasn't sure you wanted me to."
Stan lied through his teeth, it was obvious that he knew Amelia loved him right from the point he saved her. He could have made a move long ago, but something had always held him back.
It was him who had saved her.

Some irrational part of him worried that if he pursued her, it might make things awkward. As though she might one day wonder if he had saved her because he expected something from her in return. As though accepting his feelings would somehow make her love feel like a debt she owed him.
It was a ridiculous thought. He knew that.
Amelia had never been that kind of person, and her feelings for him had never felt forced or indebted. He knew she genuinely loved him.
Yet, knowing that did little to silence the small hesitation inside him.
He simply couldn't bring himself to risk making something so genuine feel complicated.
But anyways, his words made her pause.
She realized, in the small quiet way that these things settled into a person, that he had been uncertain too. That 'both' of them had been carrying it.

That 'both' of them had been reading the other's small, careful gestures, lingering looks, messages sent a little too quickly, the decision to fly across a continent under the polite excuse of work, and both had been waiting for a signal the other might already have been waiting for from them.
The realization did not feel dramatic. It felt warm.
Once the first wave of it had settled, her ordinary self began to reassemble, still flushed, still a little unsteady, but recognizably herself again.

chapters.title: Chapter 419: The Complication
paragraphs: "So," she said, a little more herself now, "you made me fly all the way to Inksea just to ask me that."
He raised an eyebrow. The lamplight caught the faint gleam in his eyes. "I didn't make you though, you were already coming."
"That's not the point."
"You could have said no."
"I wasn't going to."
The words escaped a little faster than she had intended. She paused. Stan looked, unmistakably, amused. The quiet curve of his mouth made her cheeks warm all over again.
"Don't look at me like that."
"Like what?"
"Like you're enjoying this."
"I am."
She shook her head. But she was smiling.

Their hands were, at some point, resting close to each other on the table. The polished wood was cool beneath her palm. Amelia noticed the nearness. Hesitated. Then, after a small quiet moment, she let her fingers rest lightly against his.
His skin was warm. Distinctly, steadily warm. She could feel the faint ridge of his knuckles, the subtle texture of his hand against hers.
Stan looked down. Then back at her. Neither of them said anything. He turned his hand slightly, and let their fingers settle naturally together.
That small gesture landed harder on her than anything spoken between them all evening.

Her heart raced again, but this time, she was not afraid. The warmth of his palm seeped slowly into hers. Outside, the city continued its distant, ordinary motion, but here, in the soft circle of lamplight, everything felt quieter. Closer.
The conversation continued, gently, in the small easier rhythm of two people who had just quietly stepped across a line they had both been standing at for weeks.

He teased her, at one point, about the small unaccountable urgency of a woman who had been on a plane within twenty-four hours of hearing he was home. The low murmur of the restaurant wrapped around their words like soft insulation.
She finally admitted it, voice quieter than before.
"...Maybe I did come because I wanted to see you."
He smiled. The expression was soft, almost private. "I know."
She gave him a small playful glare, though the effect was ruined by the lingering warmth in her face. "Don't get arrogant."
"Too late."
She laughed, quiet, genuine, the sound rising easily between them.

Stan's thumb brushed once more across her knuckles. The touch was light, almost idle, yet it grounded her. Then his expression shifted, still calm, still open, but something more deliberate settled behind his eyes.
"There's something else you should know," he said, voice even. "Before this goes any further."
Amelia's fingers stilled against his. The residual warmth of the moment remained, but a quiet alertness rose beneath it. She waited.
"I have other women in my life," he said simply. "Not casually. Not as distractions. There are people I care about, people I love."
The words landed with quiet weight.

For a fraction of a second Amelia's breath caught. The soft lamplight suddenly felt sharper against her skin. She could hear the distant clink of a glass somewhere behind her, the low hum of the city beyond the windows, the steady beat of her own pulse in her ears. A cold flicker of something, hurt, surprise, the sharp edge of reality, moved through her chest.
She did not pull her hand away.
Inside, the thought rose quickly, almost instinctively: 'Don't be weak. Don't walk away from something you actually want just because it isn't simple.'
She was Amelia. A Major shareholder of Warner Bros. A woman who had built her place in rooms full of sharper knives than this. She did not fold when the ground shifted. She recalculated.
She looked at him, eyes steady despite the heat still lingering in her face.
"Do you really love them too?"

Stan held her gaze without flinching. "I'm going to be honest. Yes. I do. I love them as I love..." He paused, the smallest breath, then finished with quiet clarity, "as I love the people who matter to me. I love them as I love you"
The honesty sat between them, unsoftened.

Amelia felt the competitive spark ignite, familiar, sharp, the same fire that rose whenever someone underestimated her in a boardroom or tried to close a door she intended to walk through. Her eyes glinted in the warm light, the flush on her cheeks no longer only from embarrassment.
"Then," she said, voice low and certain, "I'll make you love me more."
Stan's brow lifted slightly. A faint, almost impressed curve touched his mouth. The teasing light returned to his eyes, but beneath it was something quieter, recognition.

Amelia did not look away. The warmth of his hand remained against hers. The city lights continued their slow shimmer beyond the glass. She had not come this far, across continents, through months of careful restraint, to retreat at the first complication.
If there were others, then she would simply become the one he could not set aside.
The thought settled into her with the same calm resolve she brought to every high-stakes negotiation. She was not a woman who competed by diminishing herself. She competed by rising.
Stan studied her for a long moment. Then the corner of his mouth curved further, soft and genuine.
"I believe you," he said.
The conversation eased again after that, still charged, still new, but no longer fragile. He teased her once more about the flight, about the way she had checked her phone before he arrived.

She answered with dry precision and the occasional sharp glance that only made him smile wider. Their fingers remained loosely linked on the cool tabletop, the residual heat of his palm a quiet anchor.
Later, in the small quiet back of her own head, as she sat across from him with the low warm lamplight settling around them, a single small thought surfaced.
For once, she did not have to wonder.

She had spent so long wondering whether Stan might feel the same. She had spent so many small careful evenings running the possibilities, mapping the small hopeful signals against the small realistic ones, and telling herself, every time, not to make more of it than there was.
Now she knew.
And somehow, knowing, complicated, incomplete, and still entirely hers to claim, felt even better than she had imagined.

The residual warmth of his hand against hers, the soft glow of the lamp, the distant city lights beyond the glass, everything settled into place with a quiet certainty she had not expected to feel so soon.
For the first time in a long while, Amelia simply let herself sit with it.
And she did not look away.

chapters.title: Chapter 420: No More Pretending...
paragraphs: Amelia’s fingers rested lightly against Stan’s on the table.

The polished wood was cool beneath her palm, but his skin was warm, distinctly, steadily warm. For a few quiet seconds neither of them moved. The contact was barely anything, just the gentle press of skin against skin, yet she could feel the faint ridge of his knuckles, the subtle calluses along the edge of his hand, the slow pulse that seemed to answer her own.
Every time she thought her heartbeat might settle, the simple reality of what had just been said rose up again and stole her breath.
’He likes me too.’ She still couldn’t quite believe it.

Stan’s thumb shifted, brushing once across the side of her hand in a slow, deliberate stroke. The small movement sent a warm current up her arm, raising a soft trail of sensation that lingered even after his thumb stilled.
Amelia’s eyes flicked to his face. Soft amber light from the recessed fixtures caught the edges of his features, gilding the faint shadow of stubble along his jaw.
He was watching her with that calm, faintly amused expression she had come to know so well, except now there was something softer beneath it, something that made the air between them feel thicker.
"You’re still smiling," he said quietly. His voice was low enough that it almost blended with the distant clink of glassware and the muted murmur of other conversations.
"I’m not."
"You are."
She tried to press her lips into a straight line. It lasted less than a second before the smile returned, smaller this time but impossible to hide.
The scent of his cologne, clean, understated, with a faint woody note, reached her when he leaned a fraction closer. "You’re enjoying this far too much."
"I am," he admitted without shame. "I’ve waited a long time to see you look at me like that without trying to hide it."
Amelia’s cheeks warmed. She could feel the heat blooming beneath her skin, the slight flush that always betrayed her when she least wanted it to.
She glanced down at their joined hands, then back up. The tablecloth beneath their wrists was smooth linen, cool against the underside of her forearm. "I wasn’t that obvious.
"You flew to Inksea the moment you heard I was back."
"That was..."
"Work," he finished for her, voice dry. "Yes. You’ve said."

She gave him a narrow-eyed look. The low lighting painted soft shadows under his cheekbones, making the curve of his mouth more pronounced when he almost smiled. "You’re never going to let that go, are you?"
"Not a chance."

Despite herself, a soft laugh escaped her. The sound surprised her, light, unguarded. She had been so tightly wound for so long that the simple act of laughing with him like this felt almost luxurious.

The tension that had lived between her ribs for a long time was finally loosening, thread by careful thread. Somewhere behind her a cork popped softly, followed by the quiet pour of wine into a glass. The restaurant’s warm air carried the faint aroma of seared herbs and aged wood.

Stan turned his hand fully beneath hers, guiding her fingers into a more natural hold. His palm was warm. Steady. She didn’t pull away. The slight pressure of his fingers closing around hers sent another quiet ripple through her chest.
"I meant what I said earlier," he continued, quieter now. "I was glad you came. Not because of the intelligence, or the Vanguard updates. Just... you."

Amelia’s throat tightened. She had spent so many nights convincing herself that his attention was professional, that the way he sought her out was only because she was useful. Hearing the opposite spoken so plainly made something in her chest ache in the best possible way. The soft background music, something slow and instrumental, seemed to fade further into the distance.
"I almost didn’t message you," she admitted. Her voice came out softer than she intended. "When I landed. I told myself I should wait, that it would look too eager."
"I’m glad you didn’t wait."
"You’re very sure of yourself tonight.
Stan’s mouth curved. The corner of his eyes creased slightly. "Am I?"
"Yes. Asking me that question right here, in the middle of a restaurant, like it was nothing."
"It wasn’t nothing." His eyes held hers. In the warm light they looked darker than usual, focused entirely on her. "I just decided I was tired of pretending I didn’t notice."

Amelia looked at him for a long moment. The soft lighting caught the edges of his features, the faint shadow of stubble, the quiet confidence that had always drawn her in even when she refused to name it. She could hear the faint rustle of fabric as he shifted slightly in his chair. He looked steady. Certain. And for the first time she allowed herself to believe that certainty included her.
"How long?" she asked, voice low.
"How long have I known?"
She nodded. The movement made a loose strand of hair brush against her cheek; she left it there.

Stan considered the question, thumb still moving in that slow, absent stroke against her hand. The gentle friction of his skin against hers was almost distracting. "Long enough that when I saw your message tonight, I already knew I was going to ask. I just wasn’t sure you’d say yes with how shy you are and how hard you always tried to hide that shy version of yourself..."
Amelia’s heart gave a soft, treacherous flutter. She could feel it in her throat, in the tips of her fingers where they rested against his. "You thought I might say no?"

"I thought you might still be trying to protect whatever this was." He gestured lightly between them with his free hand. The motion stirred the air just enough for her to catch another faint trace of his cologne. "You care about the work, and various other stuffs. I didn’t know if you’d risk changing it."

She swallowed. That was exactly what she had been doing. Protecting the professional distance. Protecting herself. Protecting the version of their relationship that felt safe. The cool rim of her glass brushed her other hand when she shifted slightly.
"I was," she said honestly. "For a long time."
"And now?"
Amelia looked down at their hands again. Her fingers tightened almost imperceptibly around his. The warmth of his palm seemed to sink deeper into her skin. "Now I think I’m tired of pretending too."
Stan’s smile deepened, quiet and genuine. The teasing light in his eyes softened into something warmer. "Good."

The small movement sent a warm current up her arm, raising a soft trail of sensation that lingered even after his thumb stilled.
Amelia’s eyes flicked to his face.
Soft amber light from the recessed fixtures caught the edges of his features, gilding the faint shadow of stubble along his jaw.
He was watching her with that calm, faintly amused expression she had come to know so well, except now there was something softer beneath it, something that made the air between them feel thicker.
"You’re still smiling," he said quietly.
His voice was low enough that it almost blended with the distant clink of glassware and the muted murmur of other conversations.
"I’m not."
"You are."
She tried to press her lips into a straight line.

The sound surprised her, light, unguarded.

The tension that had lived between her ribs for a long time was finally loosening, thread by careful thread.
Somewhere behind her a cork popped softly, followed by the quiet pour of wine into a glass.
The restaurant’s warm air carried the faint aroma of seared herbs and aged wood.
Stan turned his hand fully beneath hers, guiding her fingers into a more natural hold.
His palm was warm.
Steady.
She didn’t pull away.
The slight pressure of his fingers closing around hers sent another quiet ripple through her chest.

Stan’s mouth curved.
The corner of his eyes creased slightly.

chapters.title: Chapter 421: Just Amelia
paragraphs: A server approached, the soft scuff of shoes against the floor announcing her presence.

She asked if they needed anything else. Amelia barely registered the interruption. She ordered another drink without looking away from Stan for more than a second. When the server left, the small bubble around their table settled back into place, the distant hum of conversation and the low clink of cutlery returning like background static.

Stan leaned in slightly, voice dropping. The shift brought him close enough that she could feel the faint warmth of his breath when he spoke. "You know, most people would expect a grand speech after a confession like that."
"Are you offering one?"
"No." His eyes glinted. "I prefer this. Watching you try not to smile every time I look at you."
Amelia shook her head, but the smile won again. She could feel the corners of her mouth refusing to stay still. "You’re impossible."
"You’ve said that before."
"It’s still true."
"And yet you’re still holding my hand."
She glanced down, as if only now realizing she hadn’t let go. A quiet laugh slipped out of her, soft enough that it barely carried past their table. "Shut up."
"Make me."
The challenge was soft, almost playful, but the way he looked at her made heat rise in her chest.

Amelia held his gaze for a beat longer than was strictly necessary, then deliberately looked away toward the window. Outside, the city lights of Inksea had fully claimed the evening. Gold and soft white reflected off the glass buildings in long, liquid streaks. Somewhere in the distance a car horn sounded, ordinary and muted by the thick glass. The cool night air seemed to press faintly against the windowpanes.
She felt lighter than she had in months.

"I still have to brief you properly," she said after a moment, trying for a more practical tone. Her free hand rested against the smooth linen of the tablecloth. "About the polar activity. The encrypted traffic. There’s more detail I didn’t want to send over any channel."
Stan’s expression remained easy. "Tomorrow."
"Tomorrow?"
"Tonight," he said, "I’d rather keep talking to you. Not the intelligence officer you’re trying to be because of a request of mine. I want just Amelia."
The words landed with quiet weight. She had spent so long being the reliable source, the one who always had the next piece of information ready.

Hearing him set that aside for the evening made her chest tighten again, this time with something close to gratitude. The soft instrumental music continued, low and unobtrusive, weaving through the spaces between their words.
"Alright," she said softly. "i’ll be Amelia and try not to dive into serious subjects."
They stayed like that for a long while. Conversation drifted between light teasing and quieter admissions.

She told him how often she had checked her phone after sending the message that she was inside the restaurant, the cool glass of the screen against her fingers, the way her pulse had jumped every time it lit up.

He admitted he had almost texted her the moment he landed in Inksea, then decided against it because he hadn’t wanted to seem too eager either. The mutual caution made them both smile. The faint scent of her drink, something citrus and clean, rose whenever she lifted the glass.

At one point Stan lifted their joined hands just enough to brush his thumb across her knuckles again. The slow drag of his skin against hers was deliberate, almost idle, yet it made her breath catch for half a second. "You’re still nervous."
"A little."
"Why?"

Amelia hesitated, then answered honestly. She could feel the slight roughness of his thumbprint against the smoother skin of her hand. "Because this is new. And I don’t usually... do new things without a plan."
"You don’t need a plan for this."
"Easy for you to say."
He smiled. The expression softened the sharper lines of his face. "I’ve never been particularly good at plans where you’re concerned."

That earned him another soft laugh. The sound felt freer now. She realized she hadn’t once reached for her phone since he sat down. The usual instinct to check messages, to stay ahead of the next crisis, had gone quiet. In its place was the steady warmth of his hand and the quiet knowledge that he was still looking at her the same way.

Eventually the restaurant began to thin out. The soft background music grew more noticeable against the reduced murmur of voices. Amelia glanced at the time and felt a small, reluctant pull of reality.

There were still reports waiting. Calls she would need to make. The world outside this table hadn’t stopped simply because her heart had finally settled into a different rhythm. The cool air from a nearby vent brushed lightly across the back of her neck.
Stan noticed the shift in her expression. "You’re thinking about leaving."
"I should. Eventually."
"Eventually," he agreed. "Not yet."
She looked at him. The low light caught the faint gleam of his eyes. "You’re very demanding for someone who just admitted he likes me."
"I’m making up for lost time."
Amelia shook her head, smiling. The movement made that same loose strand of hair brush her cheek again. "You’re going to be insufferable about this, aren’t you?
"Probably."
"I should have seen that coming."
"You should have."

She exhaled a quiet laugh, then grew more serious for a moment. Her fingers remained laced with his, the warmth between their palms steady and grounding. "Stan... this doesn’t change the work. The Vanguard. Everything else. I still have responsibilities."
"I know." His voice was steady. "I’m not asking you to set any of that aside. I’m only asking that you stop pretending you don’t want to sit across from me like this."
The simplicity of it settled something in her. She nodded once. "I can do that."
"Good."
Their hands remained linked. Amelia found herself studying the way his fingers fit against hers, the quiet strength in them, the easy way he held her without pressure.

She could feel the faint ridge of a scar along one knuckle, the steady heat of his skin. She had imagined this kind of closeness more times than she would ever admit. The reality was quieter, warmer, and somehow better.

When they finally stood to leave, Stan didn’t release her hand until they reached the door. The polished floor was smooth under her shoes. Outside, the evening air was cool against her skin, carrying the faint scent of rain on pavement and distant exhaust.

The Lamborghini waited under the soft glow of the streetlights, its dark surface reflecting fractured ribbons of gold and white. Amelia paused on the sidewalk, looking up at him. The cool night breeze stirred the edges of her hair.
"Thank you," she said.
"For what?"
"For asking. For not making me be the one to say it first."
Stan’s expression softened. The streetlight above them cast a gentle halo across one side of his face. "You’re welcome."
She hesitated, then added, quieter, "I’m glad it was you."

He studied her face for a moment, something unreadable and warm passing through his eyes. Then he leaned in just enough that only she could hear him. His voice was low, close enough that she felt the faint warmth of his breath against her cheek.
"So am I."
Amelia’s heart gave one last, steady thump. She smiled, small, genuine, no longer trying to hide it. The cool air brushed against the lingering warmth in her face.
