chapters.title: Chapter 422: The First Signs
paragraphs: Amelia and Stan stepped out into the cool evening air together, the restaurant doors closing softly behind them.

The city lights of Inksea stretched along the promenade in soft gold and white, reflecting off the dark glass of the surrounding buildings. Distant engines hummed. A light breeze carried the faint scent of rain on pavement mixed with the residual warmth of the restaurant’s kitchen.
Amelia’s personal car was still in another country.

The vehicles she had arrived with back then, days ago when she came to thank Stan for saving her; those rows of sleek rentals arranged alongside the Vanguard, had been temporary, booked after she flew into Velaris for the talent show.
Now that the event was over and her schedule had shifted back abroad, she had nothing of her own on the ground, at least she has nothing in Velaris and Inksea since she’s not based here...
Taking a deep breath, she reached into her bag for her phone, already preparing to hail a taxi, when Stan’s voice cut in, light and teasing.
"Why use a taxi when I’m here?"
She looked up. He was smiling, that familiar playful curve at the corner of his mouth.
Before she could answer, his hands settled around her waist in one smooth, natural motion, not forceful, not hesitant, simply certain.
The contact was warm through the fabric of her clothes. Amelia shivered once, a small involuntary reaction.

She was not used to being touched like this. Intimate, deliberate, close. Yet with him the sensation felt strangely right, as though her body had already decided it belonged there even if her mind was still catching up.
’I like this,’ she thought quietly. ’I like having his hands on me. I like how steady it feels.’

The admission was soft and private. She had spent so long keeping careful distance that allowing herself to lean into the feeling still carried a quiet thrill. His touch was reassuring without demanding anything. Secure. She did not pull away.
A taxi eased to the curb nearby, headlights washing briefly across the sidewalk.
The driver had seen them standing close and assumed the man was saying goodbye. He waited, engine idling, already calculating the short fare.
Then Stan guided Amelia toward the corner. They walked past the waiting taxi and around to where the dark Lamborghini sat under the streetlights, its surface catching fractured ribbons of gold.

The driver’s expression shifted as he watched them go. He had been circling for hours, burning fuel on empty streets, dealing with the usual thin trickle of late-evening passengers. Finally a possible fare had appeared, only for the opportunity to vanish because the man in the expensive coat had decided to give her a ride himself.
’That bastard just took my customer,’ the driver thought, frustration rising sharp and tired. ’He’s probably offering her a lift back to wherever she’s staying.’

It was not pure anger. It was the accumulated weight of a long day, fuel receipts, quiet streets, the constant pressure of making enough to cover the next tank. He grit his teeth and called out through the open window.
"Miss, you’re not needing the taxi again?"
Amelia turned. Stan’s right arm remained comfortably draped around her waist. With his free hand he raised a brief, polite gesture toward the driver.
"No. Sorry for the disturbance."
The simple courtesy took some of the edge off the driver’s irritation. The man did not recognize Stan.
He lived in the same city but rarely scrolled through the accounts that tracked young celebrities or the newly wealthy.
To him, Stan was simply another well-dressed stranger. He looked from the Lamborghini to the man standing beside it and thought, ’He’s probably the one who owns that car.’
Yet to the man surprised that the expected arrogance was missing, no dismissive glance, no condescending tone. Just a calm, almost ordinary politeness. Stan even said sorry
But despite this, the driver couldn’t help but admire Stan’s life...
The observation sat uncomfortably. ’Why does life have to be so unbalanced?’ he wondered. ’No matter how hard I work, I can only look up at people like him.’

He had spent the day driving, paying for fuel, collecting thin fares, while someone around his own age or younger could casually claim a car that cost more than most people earned in years. The world had never been fair. Being bitter would not change the fuel gauge or the next rent payment.

Envy lingered, but so did a reluctant acknowledgment that the other man had at least spoken to him like a person. The frustration settled into quiet resignation. He put the taxi into gear and pulled away, taillights disappearing into the flow of evening traffic.
Stan had already started walking again when he suddenly stopped.

His eyes widened a fraction. Something unusual brushed against his senses, Qi, not drifting idly through the air, but actively converging. It gathered toward the departing taxi, drawn to the driver himself as though answering a call from within.
’Impossible...’

The pattern was familiar. The same quiet resonance he had once felt around his sister. The taxi driver, an ordinary man with no known ties to cultivation, had somehow comprehended a Dao and gained the ability to interact with Qi.
Before Stan could examine it further, the system replied to the questions in his mind...
[He has comprehended the Dao of Life.]
[Through his resonance with the Dao of Life, he can now interact with Qi.]
[Qi is converging within his body and beginning to form a dantian.]
[The Qi is also actively tempering his body, strengthening his vitality and physical constitution.]
The implications settled quickly. The Return of Qi was not merely flooding the world with energy.
Certain people were naturally resonating with different Dao principles. When that resonance reached a threshold, they awakened and began to interact with Qi on their own.
Stan wondered, briefly, how many other ordinary people across the world might be experiencing the same quiet shift at this very moment.
Amelia noticed he had stopped. She looked up at him, brow faintly furrowed.
"Is something wrong?"
Stan shook his head. "No. It’s nothing."
Only then did he realize he had unconsciously paused their walk. Amelia studied him a moment longer, sensing the slight change, but she did not press. She trusted him enough to let the moment pass.

Something unusual brushed against his senses, Qi, not drifting idly through the air, but actively converging.
It gathered toward the departing taxi, drawn to the driver himself as though answering a call from within.
’Impossible...’
The pattern was familiar.
The same quiet resonance he had once felt around his sister.
The taxi driver, an ordinary man with no known ties to cultivation, had somehow comprehended a Dao and gained the ability to interact with Qi.
Before Stan could examine it further, the system replied to the questions in his mind...
[He has comprehended the Dao of Life.]
[Through his resonance with the Dao of Life, he can now interact with Qi.]
[Qi is converging within his body and beginning to form a dantian.]
[The Qi is also actively tempering his body, strengthening his vitality and physical constitution.]
The implications settled quickly.
The Return of Qi was not merely flooding the world with energy.
Certain people were naturally resonating with different Dao principles.
When that resonance reached a threshold, they awakened and began to interact with Qi on their own.
Stan wondered, briefly, how many other ordinary people across the world might be experiencing the same quiet shift at this very moment.
Amelia noticed he had stopped.
She looked up at him, brow faintly furrowed.
"Is something wrong?"
Stan shook his head.
"No.
It’s nothing."
Only then did he realize he had unconsciously paused their walk.
Amelia studied him a moment longer, sensing the slight change, but she did not press.
She trusted him enough to let the moment pass.

chapters.title: Chapter 423: A Little Closer
paragraphs: They continued toward the Lamborghini. Stan’s arm stayed around her waist, steady and unselfconscious.

After a few steps Amelia found herself leaning into him almost without deciding to, the contact no longer startling. The cool night air moved against her face; the residual heat of his side against hers felt quietly right.
"You always seem to appear exactly when I need something," she said, voice light. "It’s becoming a pattern."
Stan glanced down, the playful glint returning. "I already told you. You don’t need taxis when I’m around."
"Convenient for you."
"Very."
She shook her head, but a small smile remained. The short distance to the car felt easier than it should have.

When they reached it, Stan opened the driver’s door and slid in. Amelia walked around to the passenger side and settled into the seat. The interior still held a trace of his cologne. Before he started the engine he looked over at her, expression softer in the dim cabin light.
"Ready?"
She met his eyes. "Yes."

The engine came to life with a low, controlled growl. As the Lamborghini eased into the evening traffic, the city continued moving around them the way it always had, distant engines, the soft rush of tires on asphalt, the occasional murmur of passersby. Yet Amelia felt different.

For the first time in a long while she did not feel as though she were moving through the world alone. Something had shifted. Quietly. Irrevocably. She no longer felt the need to analyze it or question where it might lead.

She simply allowed herself to feel it: the cool night air against her skin through the partially open window, the residual warmth where his arm had rested around her waist, the quiet comfort of having him beside her.
Stan had gradually become someone she could rely on, not only for information or protection, but for the smaller, steadier things.
His presence made ordinary moments feel less heavy. She loved the way he reached for her without hesitation. She loved the way the city lights looked different when she was not facing them alone.
She did not guard her heart as tightly now.
And for the moment, that was enough.

Stan started the engine. The Lamborghini responded with a low, controlled growl and eased out of the parking spot, sliding into the evening traffic as though the streets themselves made way. Soft city light washed across the windshield in shifting bands of gold and white. Amelia settled into the passenger seat, the residual coolness of the night air still clinging to her skin, and for a short while neither of them spoke. The earlier moment outside lingered between them in quiet comfort rather than tension.
Stan glanced sideways. "So, which hotel are you staying at during your stay?"
"Wanhai’s HYTV Hotel."

She answered evenly, then glanced at him and quickly looked away. A faint color rose along her cheeks. Stan’s mouth curved. He understood at once. Amelia knew perfectly well that Wanhai was under his control and that HYTV was one of its subsidiaries. Choosing that particular hotel in Inksea had not been an accident. She had done it deliberately, a small, private way of supporting something connected to him. The sudden shyness under his gaze only confirmed it. He found the entire thing endearing.
"So, Amelia..." His voice stayed light. "Is what I’m thinking right?"
She opened her mouth, considered pretending she did not understand, then closed it again. Pretending would only make the situation worse. After a brief hesitation she gave a small, meek nod.

Stan’s smile widened. "Did you really book HYTV because I’m a major shareholder of Wanhai?" He let the question hang for a beat before adding, softer and more teasing, "You really love me that much? Enough to go out of your way for something this small?

Amelia’s face heated. She kept her eyes on the dashboard for a moment, feeling strangely exposed. The decision had not felt grand at the time. She had told herself the hotel was convenient, well-located, luxurious enough for a short stay. Yet the real reason had been simpler and more personal: it was his. Supporting something of his had simply felt natural. Admitting that even to herself still made her want to look anywhere but at him.
Stan noticed the deepening color in her cheeks and eased off. If he pushed any harder she might actually fold in on herself. His tone softened.
"Don’t worry. Even if it’s nothing to you, it actually means a lot to me. I’ll always be happy if my love supports me in any way she can."
The two words landed with unexpected force.
’My love.’

Amelia’s thoughts stuttered. She already knew how he felt. He had said as much earlier. Yet hearing him call her that so casually, alone in the quiet cabin of the car, was different. The phrase settled into her chest and refused to leave.

She silently repeated it once, almost testing the shape of it. How could two ordinary words dismantle her composure so thoroughly? She tried to remind herself that he had said affectionate things before, that she should be used to it by now. It did not help. Every time he spoke like this her carefully maintained defenses weakened a little further.
Stan watched the reaction and could not resist.
"My love is blushing."

Amelia turned toward the window at once, pretending sudden fascination with the passing storefronts and streetlights. She was not annoyed. Quite the opposite. She loved hearing him say it. She simply had no idea how to contain the soft, unsteady feeling it produced.

The Lamborghini continued through familiar streets. Amelia recognized the route almost immediately. Of course he knew exactly where HYTV Hotel stood. The hotel sat beside the HYTV Restaurant, a place that carried older memories for him, the confrontation with Zane that had eventually drawn Logan into the mess, and the night Zack’s girlfriend had nearly been assaulted by Damien inside the same building. Tonight those associations remained distant. Inside the car the atmosphere was peaceful, almost private.

chapters.title: Chapter 424: Her First Kiss
paragraphs: The Lamborghini continued through familiar streets. Amelia recognized the route almost immediately.
Stan’s handsome face then surfaced in her mind, her gaze couldn’t help but move to him driving the Lamborghini so casually...

Admiring his handsome face, Amelia gradually relaxed into the seat. The silence between them did not feel empty. She felt no pressure to fill it with conversation. Simply sitting beside him was enough.
She liked this version of her life: quiet drives, private exchanges, his teasing, the unremarkable comfort of having someone next to her who already knew most of her sharp edges.
Stan’s voice broke the quiet again, playful once more.
"Ain’t you my love?"
Amelia froze for half a second. She knew exactly what he was doing. She lowered her gaze, cheeks warm, and answered meekly.
"Yes."
Stan’s smile was openly pleased. He let the moment linger before adding, "You go so quiet every time I say it."
"That’s because you do it on purpose," she muttered. "You know exactly what it does."
"I might."
"You’re impossible."
"And yet you’re still answering."
She shook her head, but the small smile remained.

The conversation drifted as the streets grew more familiar. Amelia asked whether he had stayed at the hotel before. Stan replied that he knew the place better than most of its staff. She asked, half-teasing, whether he owned part of the building.
He gave her a look that said she already knew the answer and was only pretending otherwise. She finally admitted she had been aware of his connection to Wanhai from the start.

When he pressed again about whether the hotel choice had been deliberate, she refused to answer directly until he teased her long enough that the truth slipped out: yes, she had wanted to support him. The admission was quiet. Stan’s response was quieter still.
"Small gestures from someone I love matter more than expensive gifts."
Amelia looked at him for a moment, the words settling deeper than she expected, then turned her attention back to the road.
Eventually he asked, "When are you traveling back?"
"Tomorrow evening. There are things I need to handle."
Stan nodded. "I’ll try to visit your room before you leave.
Amelia’s heart gave a sharp, private leap. She kept her expression carefully neutral, but inside the thought repeated itself with sudden clarity.
’He’s coming to see me before I leave.’

The remaining time together suddenly felt shorter and more precious. Her mind wandered despite her better judgment. What would they do? Talk? Would he hold her again the way he had outside the restaurant? Would they simply sit somewhere quiet?
A more intimate possibility brushed the edge of her thoughts...
’Will we... do that?’ Her innocent mind immediately went the sex angle, but she immediately scolded herself.
It was too soon, at least that’s what she thought... Though deep within her she knew she was anticipating that, she can’t wait for that moment when she does it with the man she loves Stan...
Still, She did not even know what he intended. Yet the anticipation refused to disappear completely. She hoped, privately and a little fiercely, that he really would come.
Stan noticed the change in her expression.
"Why are you suddenly so quiet?"
"Nothing."
He gave her a knowing glance. "You’re sure?"
"Yes."
"You’re blushing again."
"I’m not."
"You’re definitely blushing."
"Focus on the road."
Stan laughed under his breath. "Yes, ma’am."

The rest of the drive passed in easier conversation, light remarks about the hotel’s restaurants, a brief exchange about how long she planned to stay the next time she returned to the city, a few more gentle jabs that never quite crossed into discomfort.

The city lights continued their slow procession across the windshield. The streets grew quieter as they neared the hotel district. Amelia recognized the HYTV branding the moment it came into view, the familiar signage glowing against the darker buildings around it.
Stan turned smoothly into the hotel’s parking entrance and found a spot without hurry. The engine settled into silence. For a short moment neither of them reached for the door.
Stan’s hand lingered on the gearshift for a moment after the engine fell silent.
The parking garage around them was quiet, lit by the soft white glow of overhead lights that reflected faintly off the Lamborghini’s dark hood.
Outside the windshield the hotel entrance waited, glass doors and warm lobby light only a short walk away. Neither of them moved to open the doors right away.
He looked at her. "I’ll see you tomorrow."
Amelia met his eyes. The playful edge had faded from both of them. Her voice came out softer than she intended.
"I’ll be waiting."
She hoped he understood the quiet weight behind the words. From the way his expression eased, she thought he might.
She opened the door and was about to step out when Stan gently caught her wrist. His fingers were warm, the pressure light but unmistakable.
"You’re forgetting something, Amelia..."
She turned back, momentarily confused. "What’s that?"
Stan’s gaze dropped to her mouth for a fraction of a second before returning to her eyes. A small, almost private smile touched his lips.
"We’ve not kissed..."
Amelia blushed hard. Heat flooded her cheeks so quickly she felt it in her ears. "I-I’ve not kissed before..."
Stan’s smile softened further. He shifted in the seat, angling his body toward her without releasing her wrist. "Don’t worry. You’ll love it... I’ll take your first kiss."
He let go of her wrist only to lift his hand and brush his knuckles lightly along the line of her jaw. "Look at me," he murmured. "Just breathe. I’ve wanted to do this for a long time. Trust me."

Amelia’s pulse was already racing. She managed a tiny nod. Stan leaned in slowly, giving her every chance to pull away. She didn’t. His lips met hers in a careful, closed-mouth press, soft, warm, almost tentative on her part.
Amelia held still, eyes fluttering shut, the simple contact sending a surprising shiver down her spine.
Then Stan took control.

chapters.title: Chapter 426: A Voice Across The Night
paragraphs: [I know I’ve been asking for much as of late, but can you get me that glassy toy you new age humans use to communicate long distance without Qi... I saw a human doing interesting stuffs with it with my divine sense and got curious...]
Stan froze. ’Camilla.’

He recognized the voice instantly. Shock mixed with sharp fascination. She had coated her words in Qi and driven them straight into his mind across an unknown distance. The technique was elegant, efficient, and completely new to him.
Curiosity overrode surprise. He wanted to try it himself.
He spoke aloud in the quiet cabin, voice low and deliberate.
"It’s called phone, and yes I can get it for you..."
At the same moment he gathered Qi, wrapping it carefully around the sound waves of his own words the way she had done, then pushed the energy outward.
The system interface flared to life in cold blue light.
[You’ve successfully coated your words with QI...]
[You’ve created the Skill, QI message...]
[Your proficiency is low...]
[Your proficiency is low...]
[You can’t send the QI message yourself...]
[Your Qi coating your words is about to dissipate...]
[Do you want to send it to any of your harem...]
Stan was still reeling from the fact that he had just succeeded at all. Without hesitation he answered in his mind.
’Yes, send it to Camilla...’
He felt the invisible Qi-coated message shoot away at a speed far faster than sound, vanishing in a precise direction.
A second later the system confirmed:
[Your Qi message has been sent to Camilla successfully...]
... Camilla stood alone on the high balcony, the night wind moving freely around her.
Far below, the city spread out in a glittering sprawl of neon and streetlight, a restless carpet of gold, white, and electric blue that stretched to the horizon.
The cool air carried the distant hum of traffic and the faint metallic tang of the urban night.
She leaned one hip lightly against the railing, posture relaxed yet perfectly balanced, as though the height meant nothing to her.
Long, silky white hair spilled down her back and over one shoulder, catching the city glow like liquid silver each time the breeze lifted it.
The strands framed a pale, flawless face of otherworldly refinement, high cheekbones, soft mouth, skin that seemed almost luminous under the moonlight.

Her eyes were a deep, vivid red, luminous and predatory, reflecting the distant neon in slow, thoughtful glints. Even in stillness she radiated a quiet, ancient power, the kind that made the air around her feel denser.
Casual modern clothes did little to hide the rest of her. A thin, loose sweater of soft charcoal fabric clung just enough to reveal the full curve of her breasts and the narrow taper of her waist.

Fitted dark pants traced the rounded line of her hips and the long, shapely length of her legs. The contrast was striking: ethereal, faintly dangerous beauty wrapped in ordinary cloth, as if the century itself were only a temporary costume.
Her divine sense was fully unfurled.

In her mind the city existed as a living map, thousands of bright threads of human activity moving, speaking, working, creating. She did not attempt to process every detail at once; even a mind far beyond ordinary human limits found the sheer volume taxing if left completely open.

Instead she selected. A craftsman finishing a delicate mechanism in a late-night workshop. Two lovers arguing softly behind closed curtains. A group of young inventors sketching feverishly on a digital board.
Anything that carried novelty or intensity drew her attention for a moment before she released it again.
The range of her sense was immense. This entire city was trivial. She had once blanketed the whole of Antarctica without strain.
Even now she could clearly feel Stan guiding his Lamborghini through the streets several districts away, and, farther still, Amelia rising in an elevator toward her hotel room.
She was calmly following those distant threads when a refined strand of energy cut through the night toward her at incredible speed.
Unlike Stan, who had tensed to dodge, Camilla simply smiled, a slow, knowing curve of her lips that softened the crimson of her eyes, and accepted the message without resistance.
Stan’s voice settled clearly inside her mind.
[It’s called phone, and yes I can get it for you...]
The words hung there for a moment while her thoughts sharpened.
’So. He truly was a master cultivator.’
She had wondered before. The glimpses she had caught of his power had always felt incomplete, carefully measured. Now the proof was unmistakable.

A cultivator still trapped in the Qi Refining Realm could never coat spoken words in Qi and drive them across the city with such precision. What she had been allowed to sense until now was only what he chose to reveal. He was hiding his real cultivation realm.
Camilla’s gaze drifted back over the glittering city while the question turned slowly in her mind.

Why? Was he concealing himself from some powerful enemy who might otherwise take notice? Or was he deliberately holding back so that the immense Qi within him would not harm the fragile, unawakened humans who still moved through the world without ever having comprehended the Dao?
The night breeze stirred her white hair again. She remained still on the balcony, crimson eyes thoughtful, and let the unanswered questions linger.
Camilla remained on the high balcony, long white hair drifting in the night breeze like strands of living silver.

Her luminous red eyes stayed half-lidded, fixed on the glittering sprawl of the city below while the last echoes of Stan’s message settled inside her mind. A few moments of thoughtful silence passed. Then she decided to answer.
Gathering a thin strand of refined Qi was effortless. She coated the single word with it the way one might slip a letter into an envelope, then released the message with a soft mental push.
"Okay..."
The Qi message streaked away at once, a faint silver thread of energy cutting cleanly through the night.

The Qi message streaked away at once, a faint silver thread of energy cutting cleanly through the night.

Camilla tracked it with her divine sense, watching the strand race across districts, over rooftops and streets, until it slipped into the cabin of the Lamborghini. The entire distance cost her almost nothing; her sense still blanketed the city as casually as a human might glance across a room.

Through that same sense she felt the moment the message reached him. Stan’s posture shifted only slightly, shoulders easing, a quiet acknowledgment registering in the way he held the wheel. A small smirk touched his mouth, brief and private, before he simply continued driving. The car’s engine remained a low, steady purr against the nighttime streets. No dramatic reaction. No pause. Only the calm acceptance of someone who had expected her reply.

Camilla’s lips curved in mild satisfaction. He had understood so quickly. The curiosity about his true cultivation lingered, quiet and persistent. How deeply was he hiding himself? And why? She let the questions rest without urgency.

A few strands of white hair brushed across her cheek as the breeze shifted. The faint glow in her crimson eyes deepened while she kept her divine sense focused. Below her the city moved in restless patterns of light and motion; above it she stood still, elegant and unhurried, an ancient presence wrapped in ordinary clothes.
She continued watching. After a short while the Lamborghini slowed.

Stan guided it to a smooth stop beside a brightly lit shop whose glowing displays spilled white and blue light onto the sidewalk, an electronics store, shelves of phones and screens visible even from this distance.
He parked with casual confidence, the same purposeful ease that marked every movement she had observed so far.
Camilla remained on the balcony, red eyes thoughtful, and waited to see what he would do next.
The sun had only just slipped below the horizon, leaving the sky in a wash of soft twilight, deep amber fading into muted violet.

Streetlights flickered on one by one as Stan parked the Lamborghini and stepped out. He remembered Camilla’s request and shook his head once, a faint, private smile touching his mouth at how strange his life had become.
The phone shop was modern and brightly lit, glass walls glowing against the early evening. Cool air and the faint scent of new electronics met him as he walked inside.

She approached with a bright, eager smile.
"You’re Stan..."

She didn’t wait for a real answer. She began moving through the displays with deliberate, sensual purpose, hips swaying more than necessary, back arching as she reached for phones on the higher shelves, leaning in closer than the conversation required so he could catch the warm trail of her perfume and the shape of her body. Her voice stayed light and inviting as she suggested models.

The contact was immediate and unmistakable. The soft, warm pressure of her plump ass pressed firmly against his crotch, her body molding to his for a brief, bold moment. Heat radiated through the thin fabric of her skirt.

She tilted her head back so it rested against his shoulder and lifted the phone, snapping a quick selfie of the two of them. As she settled against him her hips gave a small, deliberate grind, casual and confident, as if the intimacy were the most natural thing in the world.
Stan stiffened slightly. He was just about to tell her to step away.
High on her distant balcony, Camilla watched the entire exchange through her divine sense. The moment the attendant pressed herself against Stan, Camilla’s expression darkened into a frown.
She gathered a thin strand of Qi, laced it with a thread of killing intent, and sent it straight into the woman’s mind.
’Do you know I’ll kill you now if you keep doing that...’
The cold voice resounded inside the attendant’s head.

The woman froze in place, body still pressed against Stan. As an ordinary human she did not understand what killing intent was, but the overwhelming, primal fear it carried wiped every flirtatious thought from her mind in an instant.

Camilla had no real intention of killing her, the contract with Stan forbade harming humans, especially ordinary humans, but since Stan did not know this woman, a small threat felt acceptable. She realised she couldn’t stand Stan getting more girls, the feeling have always been there, yesterday night when he fucked Maya and Sophie, that jealousy grew, but she the mixed emotion of that and her pride as a vampire made things more complicated.
At this point, Stan having fun with his harem was endurable, but him getting new girls, she just couldn’t be okay with that...

Anyways the attendant feeling the killing intent and Camilla’s cold voice resounding in her mind, stiffened and quickly stepped away, then as if a switch was turned off, she became a purely professional shop worker.
The sway in her hips vanished. She no longer leaned in.
Stan had sensed the Qi message the moment it arrived. He frowned slightly, wondering what exactly Camilla had said.
He was not upset. As long as no one was actually hurt, he was fine with it. And the lady would just be rattled thinking she was just imagining things, this method was actually good...
A small, knowing smile touched his lips at the abrupt and almost comical shift in the woman’s attitude and composure.

Now subdued and slightly pale, she simply handed him the phone he had already decided on, the Samsung 20 Pro. Reliable, strong performance, straightforward interface. Easy enough for Camilla to learn. He paid without further conversation and walked out of the shop.
The attendant stared at his departing back and shivered, still feeling the residual chill of that cold voice. She whispered to herself, uncertain:
"What was that... was it my imagination?"

paragraphs: The shop felt suddenly larger after he left.
She stood near the counter, still slightly tense, watching Stan’s back as he crossed the sidewalk.

A residual shiver ran through her, the echo of that cold voice that had spoken inside her head as if it belonged there. Her heart was still beating too fast. A faint weakness lingered in her legs, the strange emptiness that followed once intense fear began to fade and left only its aftertaste.
He unlocked the Lamborghini without hurry. The dark body of the car caught the early-evening light as he slid into the driver’s seat. She could not look away.

’He was so young.’ That was the part that kept catching in her thoughts. Young enough that it should not have been possible for him to move through the world like this, quiet confidence, a car that cost more than she would earn in years, a name people already recognized.

Admiration sat heavy in her chest, mixed with a quieter envy. She imagined, just for a second, what it would feel like to be the woman sitting beside him. The leather, the low engine, the way doors opened without anyone asking questions. An easier life. A different life.
Then the voice returned in memory.
’Do you know I’ll kill you now if you keep doing that...’

She pressed her lips together. Was it real? It had to have been imagination. People did not hear voices like that. And yet the pressure had been too precise, too cold, too sudden. It had not felt like panic she invented. It had felt like something entering her mind and leaving a mark.
A flicker of leftover boldness cut through the unease. She remembered how she had stepped back into him, how her ass had pressed against him, how she had taken the selfie as if she had every right.
Embarrassment warmed her face. Another part of her, the part that had decided in a single second that proximity to him might change everything, was almost proud. She had been daring. She had tried.
It was too late now.
The Lamborghini’s engine growled to life. The car pulled smoothly into the early evening traffic and disappeared down the street, taillights swallowed by the flow of other vehicles.
She let out a soft, frustrated sigh. "I wasn’t able to get close to him..."
For a few seconds she simply stood there, the missed opportunity settling in her chest like a dull weight.

The shop’s air felt quieter without him in it. Phone screens along the walls glowed in neat rows of white and blue. The fading sound of the engine was already gone. She could still feel her pulse in her throat.
Then excitement cut through the disappointment.

’The selfie.’ A thought came to her mind and She moved quickly back to the display phone she had used. Her fingers were a little unsteady as she unlocked it, found the photo, and sent it to her personal phone. The moment the image arrived she opened it and stared.
In the picture Stan was not looking at her or the camera. He was slightly turned away, calmly examining another phone in his hand, expression focused and completely unaware.

Even so she studied the image almost hungrily, the sharp line of his jaw, the relaxed confidence in his posture, the expensive cut of his clothes, the effortless presence that had made the ordinary shop feel smaller the moment he walked in.
It still felt unreal. Someone that young should not already carry that kind of quiet authority. Wealth sat on him the way ordinary people wore a jacket, without effort, without apology.

The memory of pressing against him rose again, more complicated now. Desire and the earlier fear tangled together. The same body she had molded herself against now felt slightly dangerous in recollection, as if she had touched something she did not fully understand.
Her thumb hovered over the sharing icons.
Posting it would be so easy. She could already see the flood of likes, the comments, the envy of her followers. Proof that she had stood that close to him. That she had been in the frame with ’Stan’.
Would it cause problems?
Would he somehow see it?
Was the strange voice a warning she should take seriously?
Or was she overthinking everything because a rich customer had made her nervous?

She zoomed in on his profile, stared at the line of his mouth and replayed the brief physical contact, the heat of him, the firmness she had felt through her skirt, the reckless little grind she had given as if she were someone bolder than she usually was. She rarely acted that forward with a customer. Almost never. The memory made her cheeks warm again.
She glanced once toward the back of the shop. A coworker was busy with inventory and had not seemed to notice anything. She looked back at the photo.
The residual chill had not completely left her body. It sat under her skin like a faint warning she could not name.
She kept staring at the screen, thumb still poised, torn between the bright, opportunistic hunger to post and the quieter instinct that told her some things were better left unshared.

Stan drove only a short distance through the early-evening streets before pulling over at a small SIM card shop. The place was narrow and brightly lit, the kind of store that stayed open late because people always needed something at the last minute.
He stepped inside.
The clerk looked up from his phone, took in the black shirt, the watch, and the Lamborghini idling just outside the glass, and straightened a little.
"Need a SIM?"
"Prepaid. Data. No contract." Stan’s voice was even. "Something that won’t cut out after two hours of use."
The clerk nodded, already reaching under the counter. "How much data?"
"Enough that she can use for a long time without disturbance."
That earned a small grin. "Girlfriend?"
Stan considered the word. Ancient, powerful, and currently fascinated by a slab of glass that let humans talk without Qi. Girlfriend was not the word.
"Something like that."

chapters.title: Chapter 429: Dirty Thoughts
paragraphs: "How much data and airtime?"
"Enough that she can use for a long time without disturbance."
"Girlfriend?"
"Something like that."

Smiling heartily at what he saw as Stan trying to hide the obvious, the clerk shook his head, selected a plan, ran the activation, and slid the small plastic sleeve across the counter. Stan paid in cash, took the receipt, and walked back out into the cooling air.

Beside the Lamborghini he opened the Samsung box, slid the SIM into place, and powered the phone on. The screen lit. After a few seconds the network connected. Signal bars appeared, clean and steady. He checked once more, then slipped the phone into his pocket and set the box and charger neatly on the passenger seat.

Camilla would want to test this the moment she had it. The thought almost made him smile. An ancient vampire, curious about notifications and swipe gestures. He made sure the battery was high enough and wondered how quickly she would understand the interface.
Knowing her, not long. He started the engine. The low growl filled the cabin as he merged into evening traffic.
After he delivered the phone, he would go to Mia.

Winning Camilla would take time. Pride like hers did not fold because of a gift, even a gift she had asked for. Crowding her now would only make her pull the mask tighter. Space, after this, might do more work than another visit. Mia was different. Her presence was simpler, warmer, easier to settle into after a day that had already held Qi messages, a startled shop girl, and the lingering taste of Amelia’s first kiss. He wanted the comfort of Mia’s body and the way she looked at him without calculation. He also needed to keep the balance among the women in his life from tilting too far in any one direction. Strange days required grounding. Mia was grounding.
The thought of Camilla did not leave him.
It shifted.

He saw her beneath him, pale skin flushed pink, long white hair spilled across dark sheets, luminous red eyes half-lidded and hazy. That composed face broken open. Heavy breathing. Soft, involuntary sounds she would hate herself for making.

He imagined her on her hands and knees. One hand gripping her hip, the other coming down hard on her full, pale ass. The sharp sound. The way her flesh would jump and bloom red. He would take her from behind in deep, unhurried strokes while she tried and failed to keep her voice even.
’That’s it. Stay like that. You feel so fucking tight. Look at you, taking it like you were made for it.’
He would spank her again. And again. Until she gasped and pushed back into him despite herself.
Then her straddling him, thighs trembling as she rode. His hands locked on her waist, guiding her down onto him. Mouth at her ear.
’Slower. No, deeper. Don’t hide from me. Moan louder. I want to hear you lose it. You’re mine now. That cold little act doesn’t work when you’re this wet.’
Then on her back, legs pushed up, completely open. Him driving into her until her usual elegance was gone and there was only flushed skin, shaking breath, and the broken sound of his name.
’Filthy and beautiful. That’s what you are. I’m going to ruin that composure until you can’t put it back together. Beg if you need to. I like you like this.’

The fantasy lingered. He stayed hard the whole drive, one hand tight on the wheel, the city sliding past the windshield in streaks of gold and white. He could almost feel the heat of her, the way her body would clench when he spanked her again, the way her red eyes would go unfocused when he finally stopped pretending she was still in control.
Eventually the images loosened their hold.

City lights moved across the glass. The Lamborghini handled the road with easy precision. The cabin stayed quiet except for the engine. Busy streets thinned into quieter ones as he turned toward home.
The gate recognized him and opened. He drove through and continued into the parking garage.

The space was still and cool, concrete and shadow, the faint echo of the engine dying as he parked the Lamborghini neatly beside his Audi. Two cars side by side. His territory, quiet again after the long evening.
He sat for a moment with the new phone on the passenger seat.
Camilla would have it soon. Mia would have him after that. The order mattered. Gifts first. Comfort second. Want third, and only when it would not cost him more than it gave.
He stepped out into the familiar hush of the garage, locked the car, and took the phone and the other stuffs he got with him.

The elevator waited at the lobby with its doors already open, a softly lit capsule of brushed steel and warm glass in the high-rise’s night hush. Stan stepped in. The doors drew together behind him with a muted sigh, and the elevator began its smooth climb. Soon he got to his destination...
To his surprise Camilla was already there waiting for him...
’She came out of the balcony to welcome me, what a surprise...’
She stood a little to the side, as if the elevator were a space she had chosen. Long white hair fell over one shoulder and caught the low lights.

Her features were cool and precise until her mouth and the line of her throat softened them. Red eyes lifted to him. In the gold light they looked nice and warm contrary to the vibe it had when they first met...

Casual clothes did not hide her. The fabric followed the shape of her body without fuss. She looked out of place in an ordinary elevator. The lift hummed. Through the glass, the city lay far below in nice bright colours of the night light from homes, street light and neon light...
There was a scent to her, cool, clean, faintly sweet. Stan felt it at the back of his throat and did not step closer than he needed to.
He took the new phone from his pocket and held it out.
"What’s up with your sudden interest in phones...?"

chapters.title: Chapter 430: Unspoken Question
paragraphs: Stan took the new phone from his pocket and held it out.
"What’s up with your sudden interest in phones...?"
The question came out mildly curious, almost amused. He meant it that way. A vampire asking for a slab of glass still sat strangely in his mind, even after the shop, the SIM, the drive.

Camilla accepted the device. Her fingers were pale and sure. She turned it once, studying the dark screen, the slim edges, the ordinary weight of it in her palm. Red eyes moved over it with the same attention she might have given a talisman or a blade.
"I saw many interesting stuffs with my divine sense and got curious." Her voice was calm, low, unhurried. "Thank you for getting it for me..."

He watched her thumb rest along the side, as if she were already mapping how a human would hold it. Amusement tugged at him, genuine curiosity about something so ordinary, treated with the gravity of a first artifact. A trace of the earlier fantasy rose and receded: pale skin flushed, white hair on dark sheets, that composed face broken open. He let it pass. This Camilla, in this light, was still all control.

He took out the Uno cards next, then the chess set he had bought earlier. Both looked faintly ridiculous in the elevator’s polish, bright cardboard, folded board, the small seriousness of games meant for tables and evenings. He held them out as well.

She took them without comment. For a moment the three things sat in her hands: phone, deck, chess. Then she turned her wrist. A ring on her finger caught the light, nothing ornate, only a band that seemed to drink the glow rather than throw it back. The motion was smooth, practiced, almost lazy. Phone, cards, and board vanished as she stored them into her spatial ring... Her hands were empty again.
The small wonder of it lingered in the humming car. Items that had weight a second ago were gone. She looked at him.
"Thank you..."
"You’re welcome."
Silence settled, not awkward, only full. The elevator climbed. City lights slid down the glass in slow streaks. Her white hair shifted when she breathed, a faint movement against dark fabric.
Those red eyes stayed on him a beat longer than politeness required, then dropped, then returned, serious as ever.
After a short pause she spoke again. The formality in her voice was not stiffness so much as habit, the way a person spoke when debts were real and words were contracts.

"I’ll definitely repay you for the stuffs you got for me... I don’t have new age money, so I’m asking what’s the value of the glass toy, the Uno, and the board game... I’ll pay you in accordance with cultivation resources..."

Stan understood at once that she would not accept a refusal. Pride like hers did not take gifts and leave the ledger blank. He had known that on the drive, when he had decided space might serve him better than crowding her. He let out a quiet sigh, already tired of the argument he had not yet had.
"We’ll discuss about that later..."

The words hung between them. She did not nod. She did not smile. She only watched him, luminous eyes steady in the soft light, as if later were already a place she intended to keep. The elevator hummed on.
The city fell away beneath the glass. In the small space the unpaid debt sat as clearly as the vanished gifts, and neither of them pretended it was only courtesy.
The elevator had not yet been called again. They stood in the quiet of the landing, the high-rise’s night hush gathered around them like a held note.

Soft light lay along the brushed steel. Far below, through the glass at the end of the corridor, the city kept its muted gold. Camilla’s Qi lingered in the air, cool, fine, almost scentless, and still impossible to mistake for anything ordinary.
Stan spoke without ceremony.
"I’m heading out. Probably won’t be back until tomorrow."
Casual. No apology folded into it, no invitation for her to ask more than she wanted to. He
Camilla’s red eyes stayed on him. White hair lay still against her shoulder. The phone was gone into the ring, but her fingers curled once at her side, as if they remembered its weight.
"Where are you going?"
"Next city." A small pause. "With my sister.
The words landed cleaner than she liked.
She wanted to ask the other question. ’Are you going to see a girl?’ One of them. The warm one. The one whose name sat too easily in his mouth.
The thought rose fully formed and she bit her lip, just enough pressure to keep it from becoming sound.

If he admitted it, what could she even say? She had no claim that would survive the saying of it. Pride did not give her the right to tell him not to go. He had mentioned his sister. That was something.

She used it. Things would stay moderate. There would be another person in the room, a witness, a limit. And if she needed to know more, her divine sense could still find him. She did not have to follow. She would wait.
The lip eased. Her face did not change much. Only the faint tension in her posture remained, a stillness a fraction too complete.
Stan noticed it the way he noticed weather, present, not something he intended to name. He did not press.
"Take out the phone."

She turned her wrist. The ring drank a sliver of light. The device appeared on her open palm as if it had never left, dark screen, slim edges, still faintly warm from his pocket . She held it the way she held unfamiliar tools: carefully, without fuss.
He stepped in just close enough to see the screen with her. Not closer.
"This one." He tapped. "Voice call. You pick the name, it rings, you talk. Same as speaking into the air, except the other person has to answer."
A second tap. The interface shifted.
"Video. You see their face. They see yours. Don’t look at it like a scrying mirror the first time, it’s only a camera."
Camilla watched his hands, then the glass. She turned the phone slightly, testing the angle, the weight. Luminous eyes reflected a small rectangle of light.

The Audi’s voice was a low, even hum, almost modest. He adjusted the mirror and the seatbelt found its latch.

chapters.title: Chapter 432: The Shape Of What Was
paragraphs: He sat a moment with the key in his hand, not from hesitation, only from the habit of arriving fully in a space before asking it to move. The dashboard woke when he started the engine, pale instruments, a soft hum came with no growl.
The Audi's voice was a low, even hum, almost modest. He adjusted the mirror and the seatbelt found its latch.

Alone, the tightness he carried in other people's rooms eased a fraction. Not relief exactly. Lightness, the small kind that came with a moment alone and a clear next step. Pick up his sister. Velaris. Mia and her mother. One night. The route was simple. The evening had edges again.

A residual awareness of the landing remained, the red of Camilla's eyes, the bitten lip he was not supposed to have seen, the formal promise of cultivation resources hanging in the air like an unpaid invoice. He set it aside the way he set aside weather he could not change. The road asked for his hands.
He shifted into gear and pulled out of the space. Tires whispered over clean concrete.
At the mouth of the lot the city opened in a corridor of lights, shopfronts and signals and the dark intervals between them. He waited for a gap, then merged into the nighttime streets.

The Audi took the lane without comment, smooth, quiet, precise. Behind him the high-rise receded, a stacked geometry of windows, some lit, most not. Ahead, his sister's building, then the longer stretch toward Velaris.

He drove. The cabin stayed still except for the engine and the faint tick of cooling metal settling into motion. Streetlight after streetlight passed over the hood and sliding off again. He did not look back.

He kept to the quieter route, the one that avoided the worst of the late traffic, and let the city thin around him in layers: shopfronts first, then darker blocks of apartments, then the older streets where the lamps stood farther apart and the night had more room.

Camilla would be upstairs with the phone by now. He pictured her turning it in her palm, red eyes narrowed in that serious way she had when a thing was new and therefore deserved attention. The thought did not pull at him. It simply existed, then moved aside for the next practical piece. Sacha. Then Velaris. Then a night that needed to stay ordinary on the surface.

He drove through a district he knew by the smell of fried oil and warm pavement, past a corner store still open for no good reason except that someone always needed something late. A bus sighed at a stop and pulled away. He waited for it, then went on. The radio stayed off. The cabin was enough: engine, tires, the faint tick of the dash.

Closer in, the streets grew familiar in a different way. Not the high-rise's polished quiet. This was his sister's neighborhood, uneven sidewalks, windows lit in mismatched squares, a bicycle locked to a rail that had been there for years.
He slowed without thinking about it. The last turn came up on the left, the one with the leaning sign and the tree that dropped leaves onto the curb in every season.
He took it.
The road opened in a short, straight run. A streetlight stood at the far end like a marker. Under it, already waiting, bag on her shoulder, face tipped toward the sight of a car she recognized,
Sacha. Stan saw her before he fully stopped.

Sacha stood at the curb in the spill of a streetlight, bag slung over one shoulder, already looking at the Audi as if she had timed his arrival to the second. He pulled in. She opened the passenger door and dropped into the seat with the unthinking ease of someone who had been doing this since the car was still too big for both of them.
"You're late by three minutes," she said, buckling in. "I was about to start a rumor."
"You were on your phone."

"I can start a rumor from my phone. That's the point of living in this century." She glanced at the dashboard, then at him. "You look less tragic than I expected. That's good, seems as expected you're having fun with your 'comrade' Camilla."

Laughing at the teasing joke, He pulled back into traffic. The Audi took the lane in its quiet way. Night lay along the windshield in streaks of shop light and signal red. Sacha settled, kicked her shoes a fraction looser, and exhaled as if the car itself were a room she trusted.

"I kept thinking about their kitchen," she said, after a stretch of ordinary road. "Isn't that stupid? Not even Mia first. The kitchen. Mrs. Edith always had something on that back burner that smelled nice, like it had been there since morning on purpose. And that yellow towel on the oven handle that never matched anything."
"It was burnt on one corner.
"Because you put it too close to the flame that one time and then denied it."
"I was eleven."

"You were guilty." She smiled at the glass. "I missed that house. The way their front room always felt like it had just been lived in, it felt lively even if nobody was talking. Shoes by the door that weren't only theirs. Dad, Mia's dad, leaving the news on low like it was company. And us just... fitting. Two families in one hallway and nobody making a speech about it."

Stan drove. The memory arrived without asking: the narrow side street, the paint that peeled in the same place every summer, Mia's laugh from the stairs, Mrs. Edith's voice carrying from the kitchen as if volume were a form of welcome.
"It felt normal," he said. "That's what I remember. Not special. Just normal. Then they were gone and the normal had a hole in it."

"Strange doesn't even cover it." Sacha's voice thinned, then found itself again. "One week they were asking if we wanted extra rice. Next week the windows were dark and someone else's mail was on the mat. I used to walk past on the way to the shop like an idiot, as if the house might change its mind."
"I did that once."
"You never told me."
"There was nothing to tell. It was still dark."

chapters.title: Chapter 433: Just Like The Old Days
paragraphs: They let the conversation sit for a while as a comfortable silence descended on them and the city loosened as they left the tighter streets; lights grew farther apart.

When the silence sat too long and was getting uncomfortable, Sacha then talked about the old neighborhood in pieces, the shortcut behind the bakery, the neighbor who watered plants at midnight, the summer Mia fell off the low wall and refused to cry until Mrs. Edith appeared with ice and a look that made crying unnecessary.
Stan answered in shorter lines, but he answered. A name here. A correction there. The back-and-forth found its old rhythm, the one that did not need to announce itself.
After a while he said it almost off-handedly, as if the thought had been waiting for a gap.
"I don't know if I already told you. Mia's father died a year ago. Not long after they recalled him to the military."
Sacha turned her head. For a second the banter simply left her face.
"Damn," she said quietly. "That kind man is dead..."
The road hummed under them. She looked at her hands, then at the dark running along the window.

"He used to call me 'the general' when I made you two sit down and eat. I thought he was joking because I liked being in charge. He wasn't, not really. He was just... kind like that. Noticed people." Her throat worked. "A year. And I was walking around thinking they just moved and life got busy. That's ugly of me."
"You didn't know."
"I still feel ugly." She was silent another moment. "Mrs. Edith. Mia. God."

Stan kept his eyes on the road. "When I visited about a week ago I asked where he was. I thought I was being polite. I wasn't. I opened something they had already started closing. So tonight, don't bring it up. If they do, follow them. If they don't, leave it."
Sacha nodded, smaller than usual. "Yeah. Okay. That's, yeah." She let out a breath that was almost a laugh and failed. "I'm sad for them. That's all. Just sad."
"I know."
After a stretch he added, quieter, "We still don't know about ours. Alive, dead, neither, both. So we know the shape of it, at least. Not the same. Close enough to keep our mouths shut."
Sacha looked at him then, really looked, and the older-sister thing returned without the jokes.
"We do," she said. "We know that part."

A few more lines passed between them, low and unpretty and useful. Then the city gave them a longer straightaway, and Sacha rubbed her eyes with the heel of her hand, as if physically filing the subject away.
"All right," she said. "I'm not walking into that house with a funeral face. Mrs. Edith will feed it.
"She will."
A mile later, the smile came back, crooked.
"Is Maya still obsessed with you as she was when you and she were still kids?"
Stan smiled despite himself. "You were a kid too."

"I was the older one." She twisted in the seat, already warming to the trial. "I was looking after the two of you whenever the parents were away. You and Maya throwing tantrums like the world had personally insulted your juice cups. I was the responsible one."
"You hid in the closet during the blackout and told us the dark was a game so we wouldn't notice you were scared."
"That was strategy."
"You ate the last of Mrs. Edith's tarts and blamed the neighbor's cat."
"The cat had a history."
"You started the water fight that ruined Dad's papers."
Sacha pouted, a full, committed pout that belonged on a much younger face. "That was only a few times."
He laughed. The sound filled the cabin before he could stop it.
"Don't laugh too hard, you're driving."
"I've got it." His hands stayed easy on the wheel. "See? Control. Unlike the water fight."
"A few times," she repeated, stubborn.
He was still smiling when she jabbed the air toward him.
"And you still haven't answered. You've gotten quite skilled at dodging. Is Maya still obsessed with you?
Caught. He let the dodge die.
"From what I saw last week," he said, "she seems to have grown even more obsessed."
Sacha's eyebrow went up.
"And how exactly do you plan to handle two women? Camilla and now Maya."
He has more than two but did not correct her.
Inside, the count unspooled with dry amusement. Two. She thought two was the problem. Camilla. Maya. As if the ledger stopped at the names she could see.

He had been close with more than that, had slept with seven, if he was honest, including that one time with Vivian's sister Lily, which still sat in a category of its own. Counted properly, he was balancing around eight. Eight different temperatures, eight different claims on the same limited hours. His sister thought two would stretch him. He found that faintly funny, and a little exhausting, and not something he intended to unpack on this particular road.
Outwardly he only sighed.
"The girls I'm with love me as I am," he said. "I hope they'll understand."
Sacha heard two women in that sentence and treated it as two.

She sighed too, the practical one now. "Money can attract people. You know that. Make sure their feelings are genuine. Some women can be snakes. They smile at the car and the watch and then they smile at something else when you're not in the room."
I know."
"You're turning out to be a playboy... You know that right?"
"Yes," he sighed, "I guess with more money comes that..."
His sister fell silent for a while before saying

"I'm your sister but I don't want to headbutt too much into your personal life." She glanced at him, softer. "You're an adult. You can take care of yourself. I just get the one warning, then I shut up. Handle your girls with care."
"Thanks for understanding."

"Don't thank me like I gave you a medal. I gave you a sentence and a threat about snakes. Just the way you may or may not be using them for whatever reason you have, the girls you have may or may not be using you two... so handling many girls, you've got to be careful, to take anyone serious make sure her love is genuine." Giving that advice, She tipped her head against the rest.

After a stretch he added, quieter, "We still don't know about ours.
Alive, dead, neither, both.
So we know the shape of it, at least.
Not the same.
Close enough to keep our mouths shut."
Sacha looked at him then, really looked, and the older-sister thing returned without the jokes.
"We do," she said.
"We know that part."
A few more lines passed between them, low and unpretty and useful.
Then the city gave them a longer straightaway, and Sacha rubbed her eyes with the heel of her hand, as if physically filing the subject away.
"All right," she said.
"I'm not walking into that house with a funeral face.
Mrs.
Edith will feed it.
"She will."
A mile later, the smile came back, crooked.
"Is Maya still obsessed with you as she was when you and she were still kids?"
Stan smiled despite himself.
"You were a kid too."
"I was the older one." She twisted in the seat, already warming to the trial.
"I was looking after the two of you whenever the parents were away.
You and Maya throwing tantrums like the world had personally insulted your juice cups.
I was the responsible one."
"You hid in the closet during the blackout and told us the dark was a game so we wouldn't notice you were scared."
"That was strategy."
"You ate the last of Mrs.
Edith's tarts and blamed the neighbor's cat."
"The cat had a history."
"You started the water fight that ruined Dad's papers."
Sacha pouted, a full, committed pout that belonged on a much younger face.
"That was only a few times."
He laughed.
The sound filled the cabin before he could stop it.
"Don't laugh too hard, you're driving."
"I've got it." His hands stayed easy on the wheel.
"See?
Control.
Unlike the water fight."
"A few times," she repeated, stubborn.
He was still smiling when she jabbed the air toward him.
"And you still haven't answered.
You've gotten quite skilled at dodging.
Is Maya still obsessed with you?
Caught.
He let the dodge die.
"From what I saw last week," he said, "she seems to have grown even more obsessed."
Sacha's eyebrow went up.
"And how exactly do you plan to handle two women?
Camilla and now Maya."
He has more than two but did not correct her.
Inside, the count unspooled with dry amusement.
Two.
She thought two was the problem.
Camilla.
Maya.
As if the ledger stopped at the names she could see.
He had been close with more than that, had slept with seven, if he was honest, including that one time with Vivian's sister Lily, which still sat in a category of its own.
Counted properly, he was balancing around eight.
Eight different temperatures, eight different claims on the same limited hours.
His sister thought two would stretch him.
He found that faintly funny, and a little exhausting, and not something he intended to unpack on this particular road.
Outwardly he only sighed.
"The girls I'm with love me as I am," he said.
"I hope they'll understand."
Sacha heard two women in that sentence and treated it as two.
She sighed too, the practical one now.
"Money can attract people.
You know that.
Make sure their feelings are genuine.
Some women can be snakes.
They smile at the car and the watch and then they smile at something else when you're not in the room."
I know."
"You're turning out to be a playboy...
You know that right?"
"Yes," he sighed, "I guess with more money comes that..."
His sister fell silent for a while before saying
"I'm your sister but I don't want to headbutt too much into your personal life." She glanced at him, softer.
"You're an adult.
You can take care of yourself.
I just get the one warning, then I shut up.
Handle your girls with care."
"Thanks for understanding."
"Don't thank me like I gave you a medal.
I gave you a sentence and a threat about snakes.

Just the way you may or may not be using them for whatever reason you have, the girls you have may or may not be using you two... so handling many girls, you've got to be careful, to take anyone serious make sure her love is genuine." Giving that advice, She tipped her head against the rest.

chapters.title: Chapter 434: A Familiar Welcome
paragraphs: "Bring food in your face tonight. Mrs. Edith notices empty stomachs like a crime."
"You already told her I forget to eat."
"I will tell her again. Consistency is love."

The rest of the drive loosened into smaller things, whether Velaris still had that bad intersection, whether Mia still talked too fast when she was happy, whether Sacha should have brought something and the mutual conclusion that showing up was the something. Comfortable silence opened between the remarks and did not feel like a hole.
The streets changed. Quieter houses. Softer lamps. He turned into a lot opposite a familiar front and parked. The engine died and left them in a brief, ticking quiet.

"So, that’s their place," Sacha said, looking across the road. "It’s looking pretty good. Even though it’s not the same as their place back in Inksea before they moved here, it still brings back memories."
"Yeah..." Stan nodded.
Then they both got out of the car. Night air was cooler here, with a trace of someone’s dinner from an open window. They walked together toward the house. Sacha bumped his shoulder once, lightly.
"Normal face," she murmured.
"I don’t have a face."
"You have several. Use the one that didn’t just do math about women."

He almost smiled again. The path was short. The ugly little light was exactly as he remembered. They stopped at the door, the two of them in a small pool of it, the house waiting on the other side with its kitchen and its absences and its living people.
Stan lifted his hand and knocked.
The second knock had barely faded when a voice came from inside, soft and close.
"I’m coming.
Footsteps. A latch. The door opened on evening light and the warm smell of a house that had been cooking something earlier and had not quite let it go.
Mia stood in the frame.
She was striking in the way some women were when time had been generous and then refused to finish the job.

A voluptuous, soft figure with full, heavy breasts straining gently against a casual top, a narrow waist that flared into wide, rounded hips, thick thighs under simple clothes, the whole of her radiating mature femininity without trying.
Her face was warm and lovely. The smile that rose on it was bright and unguarded, and it took years off her at once. Skin luminous. Eyes lively.
That delight found Stan first. Sacha might as well have been part of the porch light, completely ignored as Mia stepped forward without hesitation and pulled Stan into her.

The hug was full-body and unapologetic. Soft, generous weight pressed into his chest, the give of her breasts, the heat of her through thin fabric, the faint scent of her skin and hair, something clean and a little sweet, like soap and the house itself. Her arms locked around him with familiar firmness, as if the week since his last visit had been a year. Stan let it happen. He always did, with her. She was just as she were the last time he visited, the lovely childhood friend he’d came to love, Quiet pleasure moved through him at the contact, the known shape of her, the way she fitted against him without calculation. He rested a hand at her back and felt her breathe.
It lasted long enough to be more than greeting.

Then Mia became aware of the third person. She drew back slowly, eyes drifting to the woman at Stan’s side. The more mature face snagged on old pictures, porch steps, a dry voice, an older girl who had always been her Sis. A flush of memories and nostalgia hit her hard as recognition arrived with a small shock.
"Is that... Sis Sacha?"
Stan nodded, a small smile tugging at his mouth. "Same Sis Sacha."

Mia turned and pulled Sacha in just as tightly, holding on a beat longer than politeness required. "Sis Sacha, it’s been so long... your face is a bit different. I almost didn’t recognise you. I missed you and Stan a lot..."
Sacha was already smiling. The smile had teeth.
"Really? Cause it seems you missed Stan a lot more... even though he visited you and Aunty just a week and half ago."
Heat flooded Mia’s cheeks. She pulled back just enough to look at Sacha, still holding her arms. "It’s not like that..."
"Oh?" Sacha’s voice stayed light, almost fond. "Then what is it like? Tell me. Cause it seems you’ve forgotten all about me..."
Mia shook her head quickly, still flushed, a little laugh escaping despite herself. "I’ll never forget you, Sis Sacha. You’re the one who used to steal my hair ties and tell Aunty I started it."
"And you’re the one who used to climb into Stan’s lap the second he sat down and pretend you were just cold." Sacha glanced at Stan, eyes bright. "Some things don’t change."
Stan lifted his hands in mock surrender. "I am an innocent porch visitor."
"Innocent," Sacha repeated, tasting the word. She looked back at Mia. "He still lets you hug him like that, I see. Full wrap. No escape. Very dedicated hostess."
Mia’s ears went pink. She swatted Sacha’s arm, half-hearted. "Stop. I hug people. That’s what I do."
"You hug him like he’s been gone to war." Sacha’s tone stayed playful, but there was a glint in it. "I get the polite squeeze. He gets the whole menu."
Stan’s hand found Mia’s shoulder, a brief, grounding touch. "She missed both of us. That’s what she said."
Mia seized the opening, nodding too fast. "I did. Both of you. It’s just, Stan comes more often, so the hug has practice. That’s all."

Sacha’s laugh was low and pleased. "Practice. That’s a word." She leaned in and kissed Mia’s cheek, quick and warm. "Fine. I’ll accept my second-place hug for now. But you’re making it up to me inside. Tea. Gossip. No running off to cling to him the second Aunty calls me or something."
Mia’s smile returned, bright again, a little shy around the edges. "I won’t run off."

"Liar," Sacha said, fond. She linked her arm through Mia’s and tugged her toward the doorway. "Come on. Let the man breathe for five minutes. He looks like he enjoyed that a bit too much to be useful yet. Poor me, getting all forgotten by you while Stan gets all the love..."

chapters.title: Chapter 435: The Things That Never Changed
paragraphs: "I won’t run off."

"Liar," Sacha said, fond. She linked her arm through Mia’s and tugged her toward the doorway. "Come on. Let the man breathe for five minutes. He looks like he enjoyed that a bit too much to be useful yet. Poor me, getting all forgotten by you while Stan gets all the love..."
Mia didn’t refute this time, instead she only glanced at Sacha’s face as fondness rose with the embarrassment within her heart...
’I missed these teasing of yours... it’s been so long.’
The present thinned.

Sun. A backyard that had never needed to be large. Warm afternoon light on patchy grass and the fence that always leaned the same way. Cushions, cardboard boxes, old blankets dragged from the house and arranged into a lopsided "home" that little Mia treated as architecture.
She was Stan’s wife for the day, and she was serious about it.
Plastic dishes sat in careful rows. Water and leaves steamed in her mind as soup. She checked on him the way Mrs. Edith checked on people, soft, constant, important.
"Stan, are you hungry? I made soup... well, it’s just water and leaves, but it’s special soup!"
Little Stan sat where she told him to sit, calm even then, a small stoic with grass stains on his knees. He picked up the imaginary bowl with both hands.
"It’s good," he said, straightforward, as if taste were a fact he had decided to honor.
Mia’s face lit. "You have to sit properly at the table, okay? Wives take care of their husbands."
He straightened his back a fraction. Ate another invisible spoonful. Stayed close.

Nearby, a low table had become a shop. Paper drawings served as stock. Stan had spent a long time on the money, colored pencils, careful numbers, bills that looked, to two children, like the real thing.
He held one up.
"Look, Mia. I drew lots of money. See? This one is worth a hundred."
Her eyes sparkled. "It’s really cool... you can draw really well. The numbers look so real!"
His small chest puffed. "It’s easy. I can draw more for you if you want. Or I can draw you a house. A real one, with a garden.
On the porch steps, Sacha watched with a straight face and the dry patience of someone a few years older who had appointed herself staff.
After a while she said, "Mia, you love playing wife with Stan so bad. Stan, you too, do you two plan to marry each other when you grow up?"
Little Mia went red to the ears. Both hands flew to her face.
"Don’t say that... Sis Sacha!! That’s embarrassing!"
Little Stan turned to Mia, unaffected, earnest.
"Is it a bad thing to marry me?"
Mia’s gaze dropped to the grass. Her voice became very small.
"No... it isn’t..."
He took her wrist, gentle, firm, and tugged her toward the paper-money pile.
"Come, Mia. Let’s play shop. Sacha can be the shop attendant. I’ll be the dad buying food and toys for our house with my money. You can help me choose."
They pulled Sacha off the steps. She came with a sigh that did not hide how willing she was.
Mia inspected the drawn vegetables with grave authority. "This carrot is fresh. This one is... a bit tired. Don’t buy the tired one, Stan."
Stan handed over a hundred with great importance. "I need change."
"That’s not how hundreds work," Sacha said, and gave him a five anyway.
Mia decided they also needed a toy for "their future baby." The words were out before she heard them. Sacha’s eyebrow rose. Mia went scarlet and became very interested in a paper apple.
Stan, solemn, offered her a drawn flower. "Wives like flowers."
She accepted it with both hands and tucked it into her pocket like treasure.

Then came the argument about prices. Sacha overcharged them on purpose. The two younger ones protested in unison, outraged citizens of a shop that had betrayed them. Sacha did not lower the price. She charged them extra for "talking back.
They paid in hundreds and demanded a receipt she refused to draw.

Later, when the money was a messy little pile again, Mia leaned against Stan’s shoulder while they counted what was left. Sun on their hair. Laughter still loose in the air. The safe, endless feeling of an afternoon that did not know it would become a memory.
The backyard faded.
Mia stood in the doorway of the present, Sacha’s old teasing still echoing, and warmth spread through her chest, deep and quiet and certain.
’I really do... I want to marry Stan.’
She stepped back and gestured them in. "Come in. Don’t just stand there. Aunty will scold me."

They crossed the threshold. The house smelled like itself, old wood, something herbal from the kitchen, the faint sweetness of clean laundry. The hallway was narrow enough that three people made it feel full.
Sacha’s eyes sparkled. "You left us on the step so long I thought we’d become strangers. Very formal welcome. Very... thorough."
Mia’s ears went hot again. "I was opening the door."
"You opened Stan first."
"Sis Sacha—"
"I’m only saying. A week ago he was here, and still the hug lasted long enough to file taxes."

Stan walked a little behind them, calm, enjoying the familiar weather of the two women: Mia flustered and glowing, Sacha affectionate with a knife made of jokes. He did not rescue Mia. She would not have wanted him to, not really.
"I missed you," Mia tried, to Sacha, to the hallway, to both.
"I know you did." Sacha bumped her lightly with an elbow. "I also know who you missed with your whole body. It’s all right. I’m mature. I can share a doorway."
"It isn’t, I wasn’t..."
"Mm."

Mia covered her face with one hand for a step, then dropped it, smiling helplessly, the blush still there, the house opening ahead of them toward the room where Mrs. Edith would be, and the night that had only just begun.
